Let the party give them space, offer a brief encouraging word if their friendship permits, or respond to a different choice produced by earlier play. A delay, refusal, or changed relationship is a real alternative; no outside character can consent for either of them. Their next days still include Izuku's teaching and armored work and Ochaco's counseling. This evening establishes mutual romantic intent by default, not a wedding, children, or an unwritten lifetime.

By Path at Musutafu Station District: Class 1-A and Class 1-B support old friends and make a personal commitment of their own; General Studies chooses a next ambition; Support and Management make time beyond work; Faculty chooses a life beyond institutional duty. Licensed Sidekick and Licensed Pro Hero balance service with a particular relationship. League of Villains Recruit and Independent Villain choose a future consistent with rehabilitation, custody, or continuing opposition; Vigilante chooses belonging and responsibility; Civilian Life defines the everyday life helped into being. A distant party makes its own commitment without overhearing this private exchange.

The event is complete when Izuku and Ochaco's mutual choice or earned alternative is clear and the party makes a concrete commitment for its own continuing life.

side_room_king.title: The Dorm Room King Contest
side_room_king.beats:
An evening in Heights Alliance, about a week after move-in. Class 1-A's dorm has stopped smelling of cardboard, and in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge Mina Ashido announces that rooms this unpacked deserve judging. Toru Hagakure seconds it at once, Ochaco Uraraka is curious, Kyoka Jiro is reluctant and Momo Yaoyorozu asks what the scoring criteria will be. The women of the class will tour the men's wing door by door and crown a Room King.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Izuku Midoriya tries to block his doorway and fails; every wall, shelf and pillow is All Might, and he goes scarlet while the judges count posters. Fumikage Tokoyami's black walls and skulls draw delighted squeals he does not appreciate. Yuga Aoyama's mirror ball dazzles the whole hallway. Eijiro Kirishima's punching bag and bold calligraphy are judged exactly what everyone expected. Denki Kaminari's trendy clutter is called trying too hard. Shoto Todoroki's tatami room, rebuilt in a single day, earns a stunned silence. Katsuki Bakugo is already asleep and his door stays shut. Then Rikido Sato opens his door on a chiffon cake cooling on the rack, offers slices, and the hungry judges hand him the crown. The men, Minoru Mineta loudest, demand a return tour of the women's wing; the women agree on their own terms, Jiro's guitars embarrass her and Yaoyorozu's canopy bed fills her whole room.

Sato's cake winning is only the default: a party room with a stronger showing, better snacks or a well-argued vote can take the crown, and the losers' complaints are half the fun.

By path: a 1-A student party is a judge, a contestant or both. The player's own room is ALWAYS a stop on the tour: the judges reach the player's door, the player shows it off or tries to hide it, and it gets scored and argued over like every other room, and the player gets a vote on the crown. A 1-B party hears the noise through the wall: Itsuka Kendo calls 1-B's own contest that same evening in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge, Neito Monoma insists theirs will be far more refined, and it plays the same way, the player's room included.

The event is complete when a Room King is crowned, or the party leaves the dorm.

side_club_week.title: Club Recruitment Week
side_club_week.beats:
Afternoons after classes at U.A. Academy, the week the clubs recruit. Folding tables line the Courtyard under hand-painted banners: kendo, light music, robotics, tea ceremony, track, manga, the swimming club, and a cooking club handing out rice balls. Present Mic has volunteered for the announcements and runs each club's pitch over the campus speakers as a radio segment. Mei Hatsume has set up a table beside the clubs without belonging to any of them, demonstrating a jet backpack to anyone who slows down.

The attack at the USJ is days old and the Sports Festival is close, so the fair is also the campus insisting on an ordinary week. Default course, as pressure the player can change: every club captain lights up at a Hero Course student, asks for a commitment, hears about Foundational Hero Studies, evening training and the festival, and sighs. Kyoka Jiro lingers too long at the light music table. Rikido Sato is talked into judging the cooking club's cakes. Tenya Iida reads every sign-up sheet and corrects the paperwork. Izuku Midoriya fills notebook pages on every Quirk in the demonstrations. Itsuka Kendo is claimed by the martial-arts table on sight and gets the same sigh when she explains her timetable. Hitoshi Shinso of General Studies walks past all of it with his hands in his pockets: his only plan this spring is the Sports Festival.

By path: a Hero Course party can join a club anyway and fight for the hours, or help a table recruit. A General Studies, Support or Management party has real time for clubs, and a club can become a standing part of its year; a Management party can rescue a table's failing pitch, and a Support party can end up as Mei's demonstrator. A faculty party is asked to sign on as a club's advisor and to settle a dispute over a double-booked practice room.

The event is complete when the party has spent an afternoon among the tables and signs up for a club or turns them all down.

side_rescue_training.title: Rescue Training Day
side_rescue_training.beats:
An afternoon block of Foundational Hero Studies in Ground Beta, U.A.'s mock city. Thirteen has rigged an earthquake scenario: cracked Mock City Streets full of debris, smoke pouring from the Training Building, and training dummies and tagged volunteer casualties under rubble and stranded on the Mock City Rooftops. Shota Aizawa watches from a roof with a clipboard and a stopwatch. The class rides out from the Campus Bus Terminal in teams of four, each scored on lives saved, time and clean handoffs at the aid point.

Thirteen opens with one plain rule: in a rescue, the first job is not to become another casualty. Default course, as pressure the player can change: Katsuki Bakugo tries to clear his district alone and his team scrambles after him; Izuku Midoriya, moving in quick bounds since the internships instead of breaking bones, finds a buried dummy nobody else saw; Tsuyu Asui and Ochaco Uraraka lift people out of a collapsed stairwell; Momo Yaoyorozu creates splints and stretchers faster than anyone can carry them; Eijiro Kirishima holds up a slab; Tenya Iida runs patients to the aid point; Shoto Todoroki freezes a flooding water main.

Midway the twist hits: Ectoplasm and a crowd of his clones burst out of the Training Building as a surprise villain, and the drill becomes a rescue under threat. Beating him is not the task. Teams score for keeping casualties safe and warning each other fast; a team that chases the villain and leaves its patients behind loses the most points, and that lesson is the heart of the debrief. A sharp party can still pin a clone or two while the others evacuate, and Aizawa notes who thought of the patients first.

By site and path: a party at U.A. Academy joins at the Campus Bus Terminal. A 1-A party is one of the teams; a 1-B party runs the same drill under Vlad King in the next block, or joins a mixed team for the day.

It is a supervised drill: the teachers stop any blow that could seriously hurt someone, and anyone knocked down is only winded or bruised and is pulled out to the aid point; no student is badly hurt or killed.

The event is complete when Thirteen calls the end of the drill and reads the scores, or the party leaves Ground Beta.

side_study_group.title: Yaoyorozu's Study Group
side_study_group.beats:
Evenings in the week before the final exams. The midterms left Denki Kaminari and Mina Ashido at the bottom of Class 1-A, and both are in open panic. Momo Yaoyorozu offers to tutor anyone who asks and glows when five people do: Kaminari, Ashido, Kyoka Jiro, Hanta Sero and Mashirao Ojiro. Afternoons go to the Library; once it closes, the group takes over the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge, where Yaoyorozu sets out a porcelain tea set from home that costs more than the sofa beside it and asks, in total sincerity, which tea everyone prefers.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the group works through hero law, math and modern literature with flashcards Yaoyorozu creates on the spot. Kaminari's brain shorts out on formulas, Ashido calls a snack break every twenty minutes, Sero trades jokes with Jiro, and Ojiro quietly does the most work. Across the lounge Katsuki Bakugo drills Eijiro Kirishima, shouting each answer louder than the last. A rumor passed down from upperclassmen says the practical will be against robots again, so the panickers relax about the practical and fear only the written test. By default the tea and Yaoyorozu's patience hold, and the practice scores climb by the end of the week.

A 1-A party can join as a student, tutor a struggling classmate, keep Ashido on task, or notice Yaoyorozu worrying that she is less useful than people think; a word at the right moment steadies her. The robot rumor stays a rumor, and nobody in the room knows the real exam format.

The event is complete when the group breaks up for the night after a practice quiz, or the party leaves.

side_mall_trip.title: The Kiyashi Mall Trip
side_mall_trip.beats:
A free day after the final exams, with the forest training camp still ahead. Class 1-A goes shopping together at Kiyashi Shopping Mall on Musutafu's south side: hiking boots, suitcases, bug spray and whatever Mina Ashido finds on the Fashion Floors. Katsuki Bakugo refused to come, Shoto Todoroki slips off on an errand of his own, and the class splits up in the Main Atrium.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Ochaco Uraraka goes for bug spray, and Izuku Midoriya ends up alone at a table on the edge of the Food Court. A young man in a dark hoodie sits beside him, greets him with easy familiarity and drapes an arm across his shoulders. It is Tomura Shigaraki, and the hand on Izuku's neck rests four fingers on the skin with the fifth held carefully away. He talks low: why does the whole country care about the Hero Killer Stain, and why does nobody look at him the same way? Izuku can answer only with words. Families eat lunch around them and notice nothing. Then Uraraka comes back and says hello; Shigaraki lets go, warns Izuku not to follow, and walks off into the crowd. Uraraka calls the police, the mall locks down with shoppers held inside, and Izuku gives his statement to the police that afternoon.

What the party can change: who sits near that table, how fast the alarm goes up, whether a classmate keeps the shoppers clear. Any move on Shigaraki puts the people around him in reach of that hand. He is not caught here and vanishes into the crowds before the exits close; nobody dies at the mall.

By site and path: a 1-A party is one of the shoppers and can be the one who comes back to the table. A 1-B party is buying for the same camp and gets caught in the lockdown. A party at U.A. Academy hears it from Shota Aizawa, who has had the call from the police; the class later learns that the camp destination will change and only the staff will know it.

The event is complete when the lockdown lifts and the class heads home, or the party leaves the mall.

side_pool_day.title: Pool Day
side_pool_day.beats:
A hot afternoon in the summer break, days before the forest training camp. Minoru Mineta and Denki Kaminari have a lazy, glamorous afternoon by U.A.'s Indoor Pool all planned, and talk the rest of the men of Class 1-A into coming along. Their plans fail at the door: Tenya Iida has a signed booking from Shota Aizawa for a proper training session, and the women of the class are already swimming laps with Tsuyu Asui coaching from the deep lane. Aizawa sits on the spectator bench with a whistle.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the session runs on treading water in clothes, towing a limp partner and controlled Quirk use in the water. Ochaco Uraraka floats herself a rest above the lanes, Tsuyu stays under long enough to alarm newcomers, and Mineta's plans collapse into earnest laps once Iida starts timing him. By late afternoon the men turn it into a fifty-meter freestyle race with Quirks allowed: Iida's engines churn the lane white, Eijiro Kirishima mostly sinks, Shoto Todoroki skates across his own ice, and Katsuki Bakugo blasts down the pool above the water. The heats leave Bakugo, Izuku Midoriya and Todoroki for the final. As they take their marks, the clock hits five, Aizawa blows the whistle and the pool closes; the final never runs, and Bakugo's fury is the last splash of the day.

A party can race in the heats, coach a weak swimmer, keep Mineta and Kaminari honest, or try to talk Aizawa into one last race; he almost never gives one, and a party has to have earned it.

By path: a 1-A party is part of the session. A 1-B party has the next lanes booked under the same rule, and Neito Monoma turns the race into a challenge between the two classes.

The event is complete when the whistle closes the pool, or the party leaves.

side_hero_league_baseball.title: Hero League Baseball
side_hero_league_baseball.beats:
Late summer at Takoba Municipal Stadium, lent for a day as a municipal event: the Hero League, the pros' charity baseball circuit, holds an exhibition game for disaster relief. It is the first big hero event since the Symbol of Peace retired, and the stands are full of people who need a good afternoon. Commission crews have leveled a diamond across the Exam Arena. A team of Musutafu pros, Mount Lady, Kamui Woods and Death Arms among them, takes on a side from U.A. Academy's Class 1-A. Nemuri Kayama is chief umpire, and the ground rules allow Quirks under baseball rules: a Quirk may act on the ball, never on a runner or a fielder, and giant form stays in the outfield.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Class 1-A picks positions in a shouting match. Katsuki Bakugo claims the mound, still in the news since Kamino and pitching angrier for it; Eijiro Kirishima catches with hardened hands; Tenya Iida leads off and steals every base he can; Ochaco Uraraka's floating fly ball starts a long argument at home plate; Momo Yaoyorozu manages the bench and the signs; Izuku Midoriya bats cleanup, muttering through each pitcher's habits. Shoto Todoroki's ice on the base path draws a warning from Nemuri Kayama. Shota Aizawa calls the whole thing irrational from the dugout, then starts moving fielders. Death Arms hits for power, Kamui Woods turns double plays, and Mount Lady plays to every camera. By default the pros win by a single run in the ninth and both sides line up to shake hands.

By path: a Hero Course party plays for the student side, and a 1-B party fills the bench with Vlad King's loud blessing. A licensed pro plays for the pros; a sidekick is a pinch runner, a base coach or the agency's face signing autographs in the stands. A party at U.A. Academy can catch the class bus from the Campus Bus Terminal or follow the broadcast from the dorms.

The event is complete when the last out is made, or the party leaves the stadium.

side_training_of_the_dead.title: Training of the Dead
side_training_of_the_dead.beats:
Early autumn, a school morning. Ketsubutsu Academy's hero course has come to U.A. Academy for a joint drill: Ms. Joke leads her first-years off the bus, proposes to Shota Aizawa in front of everyone and gets the usual flat no. Yo Shindo shakes every hand in Class 1-A and memorizes every Quirk. The drill runs in Ground Beta's mock city, teams mixed across both schools, Aizawa and Ms. Joke judging from the street.

Default course as pressure: an hour in, a Ketsubutsu student falls from a collapsing facade and a Quirk never used in drills goes off. Anyone bitten slumps into a slow, groaning 'zombie' who wants only to bite the next person. It is harmless, it wears off within the hour and the zombies remember nothing, but every bite passes it on. The only early end is to find the student at the center and put Aizawa's Erasure on them, and unless the party prevents it, Aizawa is bitten first, shielding a student. Eijiro Kirishima hardens and still gets nipped on the ear; Minoru Mineta seals the Training Building door with his spheres and locks himself in with a zombie; Ms. Joke's Outburst leaves the horde too busy laughing to chase anyone. Momo Yaoyorozu wants a plan, Izuku Midoriya maps the bite pattern out loud, Katsuki Bakugo refuses to be herded, and Shoto Todoroki can wall off a street in ice, though a wall that traps zombies traps bitten friends in the cold too.

At Training Ground Gamma, Vlad King runs Class 1-B's half of the drill from the Control Tower; if the outbreak spreads, Itsuka Kendo turns the Pipe Maze into a holding pen and Neito Monoma swears 1-B will catch more zombies. From U.A. Academy, the party gets the call with one order: nothing shambles past the training grounds.

By path: a Class 1-A student is in the drill from the first whistle; a Class 1-B student starts at Gamma and may be sent across as backup.

It is a supervised drill: the teachers stop any blow that could seriously hurt someone, and anyone knocked down is only winded or bruised and is pulled out to the aid point; no student is badly hurt or killed.

The event is complete when the source is erased or the hour runs out, the last zombie wakes up confused, and Aizawa calls the drill.

side_first_snow.title: First Snow
side_first_snow.beats:
Mid-December, wherever the party is: the first snow of the winter comes down on Musutafu, fat wet flakes that stick within the hour. On campus the Heights Alliance Yard turns white; in town the sidewalks go slick and the buses run late.

Default course as pressure: within minutes of the first real covering, Class 1-A is outside. Mina Ashido starts a snowball fight that splits the dorm into sides; Eijiro Kirishima hardens and takes hits for his team; Katsuki Bakugo's snowballs arrive as warm slush, and he declares that proves nothing. Someone asks Shoto Todoroki to make more snow. He explains that ice is not snow, then shaves frost off a wall until there is a soft drift, and looks quietly pleased. Tsuyu Asui does not join: the cold makes her slow and drowsy, so she wraps up in a blanket on the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge sofa and announces she will sleep until spring. Next door, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu challenges Kirishima to a snow fort contest, and Neito Monoma copies Todoroki's Quirk to give Class 1-B the taller wall.

By path: a Hero Course student is pulled into the fight or the fort contest, or keeps Tsu company on the sofa; a General Studies student finds Hitoshi Shinso walking through it alone, hands in his pockets, ignoring snowballs until one lands; a Support Course student watches Mei Hatsume field-test heated boots that melt a path across the Courtyard until they overheat; a Management Course student is already planning a snowy photo for the academy's public channels; faculty clear the walkways, Cementoss raises a low wall to keep the fight off the main paths, and Present Mic reads the weather alert over the campus speakers at full volume.

Away from campus, Musutafu has its own first snow: commuters slipping, shop staff with shovels, a dropped grocery bag to rescue. At night the flakes fall on a quiet campus under lit dorm windows.

The event is complete when the snowball fight has a winner or the party heads back indoors to dry off.

side_christmas_party.title: The Heights Alliance Christmas Party
side_christmas_party.beats:
Christmas week, evening, in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge at Heights Alliance. Mina Ashido has strung lights over every window, a tree stands by the television, and everyone wears a Santa hat because she handed them out at the door. Rikido Sato has spent the afternoon in the Dorm Kitchen on a strawberry layer cake big enough for the whole class; Momo Yaoyorozu has arrived with far too much food from a caterer her family uses. Wrapped gifts wait under the tree for an exchange by drawing lots.

Then the guests: if the raid freed her, Shota Aizawa brings Eri over from the teachers' quarters, with Mirio Togata at her side. She is small and shy in a room this loud, the youngest person there by many years, and the narration protects her. It is the first Christmas she has ever had.

Default course as pressure: the evening holds as long as nobody overwhelms Eri. Izuku Midoriya and Ochaco Uraraka kneel to talk to her at her height; Katsuki Bakugo tells everyone to stop crowding her, the closest he comes to warmth; Shoto Todoroki, asked to help, carves small ice figures for the table and gives her the best one. The gift draw pairs people at random, and someone ends up with a present that suits them terribly. Aizawa stands by the wall, refuses a Santa hat and watches Eri. The quiet stake of the night is whether she laughs out loud before bedtime. If the raid did not free her, it is the same warm, noisy evening without guests, and the class feels the empty chair.

By path: a Class 1-A student is a host and in the gift draw; a Class 1-B student hears the party through the wall from the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge, where Itsuka Kendo has organized a calmer one and Neito Monoma insists theirs is better, then goes next door to check.

The event is complete when the cake is gone, the gifts are opened and Aizawa takes Eri home to bed, or the party leaves the lounge.

side_year_end_cleaning.title: Year-End Cleaning
side_year_end_cleaning.beats:
The last days of the year, morning to afternoon at U.A. Academy: osoji, the year-end deep clean. Tenya Iida has posted a chore roster in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge, color-coded by floor and countersigned by Momo Yaoyorozu, with a name beside every surface from the kitchen vents to the bath tiles. Next door, Itsuka Kendo has given Class 1-B a fair rotation and taken the laundry room drains herself.

Default course as pressure: the roster holds until the lost things start turning up. Katsuki Bakugo, whose room is already spotless, inspects the Dorm Kitchen and orders it done again properly. Under the lounge sofa: a missing remote, three of Denki Kaminari's phone chargers and a homework sheet from April. Minoru Mineta's room fails Iida's inspection twice, and a stack of idol magazines goes into a box for recycling over loud protest. The party finds something of its own from the year, a note, a broken gadget or a photo from the Sports Festival, and has to decide whether to keep it. Neito Monoma times 1-B's finish against 1-A's and announces the result through the wall.

Elsewhere on campus, the Development Studio is the worst job of all: Mei Hatsume refuses to throw away a single baby, and Power Loader negotiates with her one shelf at a time. In the Other Course Dorm Halls, General Studies, Support and Management students share mops and a rotation nobody wrote down; Hitoshi Shinso quietly finishes the stairwell nobody claimed. In the Faculty Office the teachers clear their own desks: Shota Aizawa's sleeping bag finally goes through the wash, Present Mic cleans to music played far too loud, and Principal Nezu inspects every shelf over a cup of tea.

By path: a Hero Course student takes a line on the roster; a student of another course cleans the shared halls or the studio; faculty clear the office and sign off the classrooms.

The event is complete when the roster is all ticked off and the campus sits clean for the New Year.

side_new_year_shrine.title: New Year's Shrine Visit
side_new_year_shrine.beats:
The first days of the New Year: hatsumode. Classmates bundle up and head down from U.A. Academy to a Musutafu neighborhood shrine, where a long line inches up the stone steps to the offering box and stalls along the approach sell amazake, taiyaki and grilled squid in the cold. Some came in kimono: Momo Yaoyorozu in a formal furisode her family sent, Mina Ashido and Toru Hagakure in rented ones (Toru's appears to walk on its own, and the shrine attendants stare), Ochaco Uraraka in her warmest coat and nothing new.

Default course as pressure: Tenya Iida has planned the visit to the minute and loses half the group at the first stall. At the offering box each tosses a coin, rings the bell, claps twice and wishes. Ochaco wishes for her parents' business; Izuku Midoriya wishes longer than anyone and will not say what for; Katsuki Bakugo claps once, hard, and walks off. Then the fortunes: Denki Kaminari draws great misfortune and ties it to the rack in a panic; Eijiro Kirishima draws great blessing and offers to share it, because that is the manly thing to do; Tsuyu Asui hides in her scarf and says the cold is making her sleepy. Wishes go up on wooden ema plaques, reading someone else's is rude, and someone does anyway.

Class 1-B is in the line too. It is Pony Tsunotori's first Japanese New Year, so she asks about everything and repeats each step aloud; Itsuka Kendo explains, and Neito Monoma compares fortunes with 1-A until one of his is worse.

By path: a Hero Course student is in either group; a General Studies student may find Hitoshi Shinso alone near the back of the line; a Support Course student sees Mei Hatsume buy a charm for luck with sponsors; a Management Course student notes which hero goods the stalls are selling, Endeavor masks most of all.

The party's wish and fortune are the player's to choose; a fortune sets a mood and never foretells anything.

The event is complete when the party has prayed, drawn a fortune and eaten something hot from the stalls.

side_valentines.title: Valentine's Day
side_valentines.beats:
February 14, a month after the Paranormal Liberation War. Whatever the war cost U.A. Academy, the campus wants an ordinary day, and Valentine's Day is ordinary in the loudest way: chocolate everywhere, most of it obligation chocolate, plenty of it friendship chocolate, little of it anything more.

Default course as pressure: Rikido Sato ran a chocolate workshop in the Dorm Kitchen last night, and half the dorm's gifts came out of it. Momo Yaoyorozu gives a box of imported truffles to every classmate and every teacher and is baffled when asked if one means something. Mina Ashido runs a friendship-chocolate swap; Toru Hagakure's boxes seem to float down the hall. Minoru Mineta waits by his desk all day, receives only the class-wide boxes, and calls them proof the universe hates him. Shoto Todoroki receives a pile from strangers and asks, sincerely, what he is supposed to do with it. Pony Tsunotori explains that back home anyone gives anyone a card, and gives everyone one.

Quiet moments: Ochaco Uraraka wraps one box twice and leaves it in her bag. If Katsuki Bakugo is still on strict rest in the dorm, Eijiro Kirishima brings up the boxes sent to him; Katsuki tells him to eat them and keeps one. If Nemuri Kayama did not come back from the war, students leave small chocolates on her desk in the Faculty Office, and nobody moves them. If Shota Aizawa is back on campus, he finds obligation chocolate on his desk signed by all of Class 1-A and pretends not to.

By path: a Hero Course student gives, gets or dodges chocolate; a General Studies student sees Hitoshi Shinso handed an unexpected box; a Support Course student watches Mei Hatsume present Power Loader with a chocolate-tempering machine she calls her newest baby; a Management Course student tracks which hero-brand chocolates sell out.

What the party gives, and to whom, is the player's choice; romance stays a hint unless the player speaks it.

The event is complete when the chocolate has changed hands and the day ends.

side_white_day.title: White Day
side_white_day.beats:
March 14, White Day: a month after Valentine's, whoever received chocolate returns the favor, ideally with something sweeter and, by a rule nobody can trace, worth three times as much. The school year is nearly over, the third-years' graduation is close and spring break hangs over both Hero Course classes.

Default course as pressure: Tenya Iida has a spreadsheet of who gave what, what a triple return would cost and a bow rehearsed for each name. Shoto Todoroki takes the three-times rule literally and returns three of everything. Katsuki Bakugo, who cooks better than he admits, leaves a tray of perfect homemade cookies on the lounge table with a note reading "Don't make it weird" and is gone before anyone can thank him. Rikido Sato bakes for everyone who came to his February workshop. Minoru Mineta returns his class-wide chocolate with a long, formal speech. Denki Kaminari forgot entirely and sprints to the Campus Store at lunch. Eijiro Kirishima hands out his returns with a fist bump each. In Class 1-B, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu tears up over a card of thanks, and Neito Monoma gives returns to all of 1-B and, after a long pause, leaves one unsigned box outside 1-A's door.

The heart of the day is thanks that matter: a small return to someone who helped the party through the winter, a classmate who sat by a hospital bed, or a friend who never asked for anything. Friendship first; anything more stays a hint unless the player speaks it.

By path: a Hero Course student gives and receives returns in the dorm and the homerooms; a General Studies student sees Hitoshi Shinso return a February box in person with one awkward, honest line; a Support Course student is offered a free gear upgrade by Mei Hatsume as her version of a return, wanted or not; a Management Course student watches the Campus Store's White Day stock sell out by noon.

The event is complete when the returns are given, the thanks said and the day winds down.

pro_rent_day.title: Rent Day
pro_rent_day.beats:
Mid-April, in the days after the League of Villains' attack on the USJ made national news. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: the agency phone rings with the office manager on the line, or three envelopes wait on the front desk. The landlord wants to discuss the month's rent and a clause about damage to the shared garage; the accountant needs signatures for payroll and warns that the liability insurer has raised its premium since the USJ attack; and a sponsor's representative, a local business paying for a logo on the costume, has booked the quarterly check-in and wants photos, patrol numbers and a word about any complaints.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: all three meetings land on the same afternoon, an hour apart, and dispatch calls a fight near the station between the second and the third. The party can hold each meeting, move one, send someone, bargain, or take the call and let the paperwork wait. Money moves only through what is agreed: a late payment brings a written notice and a fee, never an eviction this week; a sponsor who gets no photos cuts the next payment; an honest account of a complaint keeps a sponsor more often than a dodge does.

An agency head sits across the table from all three and decides who gets paid first. A sidekick works for someone: the boss is tied up and sends the sidekick to the sponsor in costume to smile and answer for the patrol numbers, or the sidekick's pay arrives a day late with an apology from the office manager, and the sidekick decides whether to raise it. On Hero Agency Row the Ready Room trades bills: Mount Lady calls her damage bills a marketing cost, and Gunhead, down the hall, quietly names an insurer who treats small agencies fairly. At a Tokyo agency the rent is higher and the sponsor wants the logo on camera under the giant screens.

The event is complete when the three meetings are held, moved or skipped and the agency's money for the month is settled one way or another.

pro_festival_scouting.title: Scouting the Sports Festival
pro_festival_scouting.beats:
The two days off after the U.A. Sports Festival, afternoon into night. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: the agency inbox chimes with U.A.'s internship offer form, due back before Friday's Hero Name Day, while every channel replays the first-year events. By evening the agency's people crowd a screen with takeout and argue picks.

The replays show only what happened in public; by canon default, unless the story changed it: Katsuki Bakugo won the tournament over a Shoto Todoroki who held back his fire in the final; Izuku Midoriya won the obstacle race and wrecked his fingers against Todoroki; Ochaco Uraraka refused to quit against Bakugo; Hitoshi Shinso of General Studies nearly brainwashed his way past Izuku; Fumikage Tokoyami and Tenya Iida placed third, though Iida left the stadium after his semifinal when word came that his brother Ingenium had been attacked in Hosu. Commentators agree the famous names will drown in offers.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: the staff split between a famous name that will never say yes to a small agency and a student who lost early but did one thing well on camera, and the form takes one name, several, or none. An offer costs nothing to send; hosting costs a week of supervision, and the supervising pro answers for everything the intern does. Offers go to Hero Course first-years of Class 1-A and 1-B; support companies, not agencies, chase the Support Course's inventors.

An agency head hears the arguments and signs the form. A sidekick works for someone: the boss wants a written scouting note on one student by morning, and the sidekick's pick can win the argument or lose it. On Hero Agency Row, Fourth Kind has already sent his and will not say whom, and Mount Lady asks which student would look good beside her on camera. A Tokyo agency's scout sat in the stands and has opinions on everyone.

The event is complete when the agency's offers are sent, or it decides to send none, before Hero Name Day.

pro_intern_host.title: Hosting an Intern
pro_intern_host.beats:
Internship week begins, morning. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: the front desk calls to say a U.A. first-year is waiting in the lobby in hero costume, or the student phones from the station asking the way. The intern is the first-year who accepted the agency's offer after Hero Name Day; if the agency sent none or nobody accepted, U.A. places one from its list of agencies that take interns. Students whose records name another host, Izuku Midoriya, Tenya Iida and Shoto Todoroki among them, go there and never here. The intern gives the hero name chosen on Hero Name Day and acts as their record describes.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: forms first. The supervising pro signs for the week and answers for anything the intern does; on duty the intern may use a Quirk only on a direct order. Then a costume check, the agency's rules, and a first patrol of the beat, where a small real case breaks: a shoplifter with a slippery Quirk, a delivery van wedged in a narrow street with its driver trapped behind a jammed door, a commuter fallen on a station stair. The intern wants to act before the order comes, and how the supervisor answers sets the tone of the week.

An agency head signs as supervisor, sets the week's plan and takes a call from U.A. checking on the placement. A sidekick works for someone: the boss hands the intern to the sidekick for the patrol, and the report afterward goes to the boss with both names on it. On Hero Agency Row the neighbors' interns arrive the same week, and comparisons start in the Ready Room. At a Tokyo agency the intern arrives rattled by the crowds at the crossing and keen not to show it.

The event is complete when the intern's first patrol ends and the first incident report is filed, or the agency sends the intern back to U.A.

pro_hero_killer_alert.title: Hero Killer Alert
pro_hero_killer_alert.beats:
The nights after the Hosu Incident, evening into late night. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: the Commission's incident app pushes a notice, and the agency radio repeats it. The Hero Killer alert issued after Ingenium was cut down in Hosu on Sports Festival day stays in force for the week: pros patrol in pairs after dark, check in by radio every twenty minutes and stay off lone rooftops.

By canon default, unless the story changed it, Stain was captured in Hosu and the official account credits Endeavor; the alert stands because footage of Stain demanding true heroes spreads faster than the police can pull it, and the Commission fears his admirers. If the story left Stain free, the alert is for him, and he is not caught tonight: whoever glimpses him sees a ragged red scarf on a far roofline, gone before backup arrives.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: a quiet paired patrol, a partner's check-in missed with no answer, and a run to the last reported spot. The cause is ordinary, a dead radio battery or a fall on a fire escape, and the scare that follows is not: a bitter young man in a red scarf, a kitchen knife in his hand, quoting the footage at a pro on a back street. He can be talked down, restrained or lost in the alleys; nobody here is the Hero Killer.

An agency head writes the pairing roster, takes a pair or sends the sidekick out, and answers to the Commission for every missed check-in. A sidekick works for someone: the boss sets the pair and the route, and the sidekick either reports the missed check-in up the chain or goes first and explains in the report. On Hero Agency Row, Death Arms and Backdraft pair by habit, and the roster puts the party beside a neighboring agency's sidekick. In Tokyo the alert sits heavier, with Hosu a short train ride north.

The event is complete when the night's patrol ends with every pair checked in and the scare answered, or the alert is lifted.

pro_disaster_drill.title: The Regional Disaster Drill
pro_disaster_drill.beats:
Mid-May, a weekday morning. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: the Commission's incident app posts the agency's slot in the regional disaster-response drill, required of every licensed agency in the district, with a staging time that morning. The site is a block of condemned buildings at the edge of the city, rigged with rubble, smoke machines and sirens. The scenario is a major earthquake: three collapsed buildings, a ruptured gas main marked by flags, and casualties played by Commission staff and trained actors carrying cards that list their injuries. Police run the cordon, the fire service holds the command post, paramedics wait at the triage tent, and a Commission evaluator with a tablet grades each agency on coordination, not captures.

The default course, as pressure the player can change: every agency talks on the radio at once and the net jams; two agencies claim the same building and search it twice while a third stands idle; an aftershock signal clears everyone out mid-search; then a wall that was never meant to fall shifts for real and pins a firefighter's leg. The evaluator calls the code that halts the drill, and the real rescue is the one that counts.

An agency head commands a sector, reports to the fire chief, sets the triage order and answers for the agency's grade. A sidekick works for someone: the sidekick leads a search team under the boss's orders, finds the shifting wall first and decides whether to call it up the chain or act. If the agency is on Hero Agency Row, the Row's agencies drill together: Backdraft works beside the fire service and counts heads, and Death Arms shifts debris wherever he is pointed. A Tokyo agency drills in a larger zone, with twice as many agencies on the same channel.

The event is complete when the all-clear sounds and the evaluator hands the agency its grade, or the drill is halted and everyone is out of the rubble.

pro_spring_chart.title: The Spring Billboard Release
pro_spring_chart.beats:
The spring Hero Billboard Chart JP release, at the turn of May into June, late afternoon into night. The scene reaches the party wherever it is: phones buzz at once with the Commission's release, and every screen and radio carries it. The chart ranks heroes by incidents resolved, public approval and social contribution, and its top holds no surprise: All Might Number One, Endeavor Number Two for yet another half year, Hawks third and Best Jeanist fourth. Commentators spend the evening on whether anyone will ever close the gap at the top.

The agency's own place sits deep in the lower pages, and it moves only through what the party actually did since the start of the year: captures, rescues, any drill grade, complaints on file. A new agency's first appearance counts, and so does a drop. The default course, as pressure the player can change: within the hour two sponsors call about the number, one to raise a fee and one to ask about a clause; a local reporter wants a comment by morning; and a box of fan mail arrives with a crayon drawing of the costume among the letters.

An agency head takes the sponsor calls and decides what to say to the reporter and what to tell the sidekick. A sidekick works for someone: the chart ranks the hero on the door, not the sidekick, yet one letter in the box is addressed to the sidekick by hero name, and the boss's mood after the number follows the sidekick through the evening shift. On Hero Agency Row the Ready Room compares ranks: Kamui Woods' steady rise draws a loud reply from Mount Lady, and Fourth Kind says one word about his own number. A Tokyo agency measures its rank against the agencies it fights for camera time.

The event is complete when the chart is out, the agency has answered its first sponsor call about it, and the evening's mail is read or left for morning.

pro_talk_show.title: Talk Show Appearance
pro_talk_show.beats:
Early summer in Tokyo, afternoon or evening. Weeks ago a network booked the party: a guest seat on a live talk show at the Tokyo Broadcasting Center, or a sponsor's photo shoot under the giant screens of Central Tokyo Streets. All Might is Number One and teaching at U.A. Academy, the League of Villains has been on every panel since the USJ attack, and the Hosu incident is weeks old: the public account says Endeavor caught Stain, the Hero Killer, and his words about false heroes keep spreading online.

At the Tokyo Broadcasting Center security has the booking and waves the party in; a runner collects it in the Broadcast Center Lobby and walks it to the Studio Floor. Uwabami is shooting a commercial on the white backdrop next door; between takes she rates the party's camera presence out loud. The host, a generated personality the narration names, is warm on air and fishing: does the party agree with Stain that heroes work for money, did Endeavor really catch him, what does a small agency earn. The sponsor's rep wants the logo in every shot and a pose on cue.

On Central Tokyo Streets the shoot runs on Billboard Avenue with a photographer, a reflector crew and a wall of phones; Edgeshot and Yoroi Musha are at a signing on the Department Stores row. Canon default pressure: mid-shoot, a real incident breaks at the Scramble Crossing and Mirko drops from a rooftop to take it; whether the party drops the pose and works it, shares it or leaves it to her is the clip that runs tonight.

An agency head carries the agency's image: every answer is a sponsor decision and a line in tomorrow's news. A sidekick is booked beside the boss or for a clip that went around online, and the host keeps asking what the boss is really like. A careless line about Stain or a fellow pro becomes a headline; a good one wins fans. Nobody on set knows anything about Hosu beyond the news.

The event is complete when the segment wraps or the shoot ends and the party has given the camera its answer.

pro_team_up_raid.title: The Team-Up Raid
pro_team_up_raid.beats:
A late-July evening. The request reaches the party on the agency radio or the Commission's incident app: police hold a warrant for a warehouse where a broker sells unlicensed support gear (modified gauntlets, fake agency costumes, police-band scanners) to bag snatchers and crews who want to fight heroes, and several agencies are asked to join tonight's raid. Since the USJ attack and the Nomu in Hosu, police want illegal gear off the streets. The broker, his staff and his buyers are generated people.

The briefing runs in a police station's back room: a floor plan, three doors, a loading bay on a canal, and an officer who wants the stock intact as evidence. Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the breach goes to plan for about a minute. Then the night guard, whose Quirk swallows all sound in a wide circle, steps out and every radio goes dead; a buyer straps on a gauntlet he never tested and blows a row of shelving into the aisle; the broker runs for the loading bay with the ledger that would convict him.

If the party's agency works Musutafu, the partners are its Hero Agency Row neighbors: Death Arms first through the door shouting warnings, Backdraft counting heads and dousing the sparks, Gunhead with a quiet restraint, Fourth Kind giving one terse order, Kamui Woods binding buyers while Mount Lady, too big for the aisles, waits at the canal for whoever runs. Sansa Tamakawa holds the warrant and takes statements. Elsewhere the partners are generated working pros and local police.

A sidekick takes the post the boss assigns (a rear door, the bay, the perimeter) and decides how far to go once the radios die. An agency head argues for a role at the briefing, commits the sidekick and signs the team-up form. Who made which arrest goes on the Commission's record and decides the pay, and the argument over credit starts at once.

The event is complete when the warehouse is secured and the credit is logged, or the broker gets away with the ledger.

pro_charity_gala.title: The Charity Gala
pro_charity_gala.beats:
Tonight, an evening in early September, in a hotel ballroom in central Tokyo. The party accepted the invitation weeks ago and the scene opens as it arrives in formal wear: cut straight to the ballroom, with no travel, briefing or other case first. It is a charity gala for the residents of Kamino Ward, whose blocks were flattened on live television. It is the first big hero event since All Might retired; his portrait stands by the stage and every toast mentions him. Endeavor, now the highest-ranked active hero, sends a large check and no speech, and the room talks about him all night. Best Jeanist's table keeps an empty chair while he recovers from Kamino, unless the story spared him.

Uwabami runs the auction in an evening gown: signed goods, a day on patrol with a ranked pro, a framed poster from All Might's debut year, sponsors bidding against each other. Edgeshot, who fought at Kamino, accepts one toast, credits the heroes beside him and leaves early. Yoroi Musha sits upright in formal dress, unimpressed by all of it. Sponsors' reps work the tables, and reporters ask every pro whether anyone can fill the gap.

Canon default pressure: near the end, trouble at the entrance. A Kamino resident who lost his shop shouts at the arriving guests, a man quoting Stain throws paint over a pro's car, security shoves back, and phones film everything. Unless someone steps in well, the crowd outside turns on the heroes and the clip runs under tomorrow's headlines.

An agency head is a guest with a sponsor table to charm, an auction paddle and a budget that cannot cover the lot it wants; a bid or a few words at the microphone get noticed. A sidekick comes as the boss's plus-one and hears a bigger agency sound them out over dessert, or works the door with the security detail and is first to the trouble.

The event is complete when the auction closes and the trouble at the entrance is settled, one way or another.

pro_tartarus_escort.title: The Tartarus Transfer Escort
pro_tartarus_escort.beats:
Early October, before dawn. The order reaches the party on the agency radio and the Commission's incident app: since All Might retired and petty crime rose, the police are short of escorts, and the agency is assigned to guard a convicted villain from a police holding center to the Tartarus Transfer Port, a drive of under two hours. The prisoner is a generated man the narration names once: his attacks crippled two pros, his Quirk is too dangerous for an ordinary prison, and he rides sealed in Quirk-blocking restraints. Port guards are on edge; the masked villain from Kamino sits on the island now.

Two armored police vans, a lead car and the party. The prisoner talks the whole way: offers money, names a stash, needles the youngest officer, asks what a world without All Might pays a hero. Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: on the coast road a staged crash blocks a tunnel, the prisoner's old crew waits to cut him out, stalled drivers film from their cars, and a warning light on his restraints starts to flicker. The escort can push through, reroute, call local pros or fight; anything that puts the trapped drivers at risk costs the agency dearly.

At the Port Security Gate, prefectural police check every name against the manifest and turn back anyone not on it. In the Transfer Waiting Hall the board says the boat is late in rough seas, and the prisoner tries one last deal. At the Transfer Pier guards walk him aboard in full restraints and the party signs him over; nobody from the escort goes to the island.

A sidekick rides in the back of the van with the prisoner or drives the lead car, with the boss on the radio and the prisoner working on the weakest nerve in the van. An agency head plans the route and formation, signs the custody form and answers to the Commission for anything that goes wrong.

The event is complete when the prisoner is signed over at the pier, or escapes on the way.

pro_license_audit.title: The License Audit
pro_license_audit.beats:
A weekday morning in early November. The notice lands on the Commission's incident app at breakfast: an audit of the party's license and agency records, today, and an inspector already on the way. Since the Shie Hassaikai raid the Commission has been checking how agencies document joint work with the police, and with the first Billboard Chart since All Might retired still ahead, it wants every file clean. The inspector is a generated Commission official the narration names: polite, tireless, armed with a tablet and a checklist.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the inspector settles at the agency's front desk and works through the files. Two summer capture reports lack a police case number; a property-damage claim from the spring was settled without the form the Commission requires; and one closed case is reopened, a capture where a witness now says the suspect was already down when the party struck. The inspector wants the missing forms by end of day and a statement on the reopened case. A lie in the paperwork surfaces sooner or later.

The forms mean calls to a police front desk, an old witness and a sponsor's lawyer, or a trip to the Licensing Bureau at the Hero Public Safety Commission Headquarters, where clerks process sidekick contracts and Yokumiru Mera, buried in exam reports, may sign one off after a remark about how little he slept.

A sidekick's own license file is on the table: a Quirk registration out of date, a report the boss signed without reading, and a boss who may cover for the party or let the party carry it. An agency head answers for everything: the books, the insurance, the sidekick contracts and the settled claim. A bad finding means a fine, a lower approval score before the chart or a suspended license.

The event is complete when the inspector files a finding: clean, a warning, or a referral to a review hearing.

pro_sidekick_poaching.title: Poached
pro_sidekick_poaching.beats:
A weekday in mid-December. The first chart without All Might ranked Endeavor Number One and Hawks Number Two, and the High-End fight over Fukuoka, carried live, made the whole country watch the new Number One bleed and win. Agencies that climbed the chart are hiring hard. One of them, a generated agency from a bigger city with a fresh billboard and a recruiter the narration names, makes its move. It reaches the party as a lunch invitation at a good restaurant, a card left at the coffee stand by the agency door, or a message on a personal phone.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the recruiter offers better pay, a patrol district of one's own, camera time and a deadline at the end of the week. The bigger agency's head joins by video call to make it personal. Word of the offer reaches the rest of the agency before the deadline, and everyone has an opinion.

A sidekick is the one being courted. The offer is real, and the boss hears of it from the party or from gossip; the boss may counter with money the agency barely has, or with a promise. Loyalty, pay and ambition pull different ways. Taking the job means a new agency from the new year; staying means telling the recruiter no.

An agency head learns the recruiter is after the agency's best sidekick, the one the party relies on most; or the offer is to the head: fold the agency into the bigger one as a branch office, keep the name on the door in small print and stop worrying about rent. A counter-offer costs money; a speech costs nothing and may not be enough. The generic sidekick has reasons of their own and says them, and nobody is forced either way.

The event is complete when the deadline passes or the offer is accepted or refused, and the agency knows who is staying.

side_intern_day_one.title: Internship Week: Day One
side_intern_day_one.beats:
The first morning of internship week, at the agency the party chose in the Internship Week quest. The party reports in hero costume, with the hero name from Hero Name Day on every form. The mentor is the pro the party picked, played as that pro's record describes; at an agency without a record, a working pro and a small staff of the narration's making. Classmates are at their own agencies, and the class group chat lights up by breakfast: Eijiro Kirishima posts a photo of Fourth Kind's Ready Room, and Ochaco Uraraka reports that Gunhead is far gentler than his mask.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the mentor sets the rules before anything else. An intern observes and assists, follows orders on duty, wears the costume in public and uses a Quirk in a fight only when a life is at stake; there is no license, and the mentor signs for every mistake. Then the tour: front desk, locker room, radio room, the wall map of the beat. Then paperwork, more than anyone at U.A. warned about: insurance, a Quirk-use declaration, a badge photo. After lunch the mentor walks the first patrol route and points out what matters: a station exit where pickpockets work, a bridge that jams at rush hour, a shopkeeper who always calls the agency first. On that walk something small happens (a lost tourist, a fender-bender, a fan who wants a photo with the new intern), and whether the party acts at once or waits for the word decides how the mentor reads the rest of the week.

If the party chose a classmate's canon host, that classmate is a fellow intern this week. By path: a 1-A party trades first-day stories in the 1-A chat. A 1-B party hears from its own: Itsuka Kendo is at Uwabami's beside Momo Yaoyorozu, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu at Fourth Kind's beside Kirishima, and the 1-B chat turns into a contest over whose agency is tougher.

The event is complete when the first patrol route has been walked and the mentor dismisses the party for the day, or sends it back to U.A.

side_intern_patrol.title: Internship Week: Night Patrol
side_intern_patrol.beats:
A night in the middle of internship week, on supervised patrol with the mentor through the agency's city. The Hero Killer is in every news crawl: days ago he attacked Ingenium, Tensei Iida, the popular head of Team Idaten, and pros across the country now patrol in pairs after dark. The mentor raises it once, flatly: an intern stays at the mentor's side, and nobody chases a name from the news. The Hero Killer never appears in this scene, whatever city the agency works.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the first hours are quiet, a slow walk of the beat, a convenience-store clerk with a question, a mentor's story about the first year on the job. Then the radio calls something real, picked to fit the agency's city and work: a mugging in a covered arcade, a fire in a noodle shop with an apartment above it, a drunk whose Quirk has torn a vending machine off the wall. The mentor takes the dangerous part and gives the party a post: keep the street clear, guide residents down the back stairs, hold the crowd behind the tape, watch one exit.

Then the post is tested. A resident appears at a window the mentor has not seen, a suspect bolts straight past the party's position, or a bystander with a phone pushes under the tape for a better shot. A life at stake justifies acting without the order, and the mentor says so afterward; leaving the post to chase a thief earns a sharp lecture, however well it turns out. Police take the scene, and the mentor walks the party through the incident report line by line, because an intern's account goes on the record.

By path: a 1-A or 1-B party works the same rules. Back at the agency the class chat is full of other people's patrols, and the mentor wants the report finished before anyone checks a phone.

The event is complete when the call is resolved and the incident report is signed, or the mentor ends the patrol early.

side_intern_evaluation.title: Internship Week: The Evaluation
side_intern_evaluation.beats:
The last day of internship week, from midday into the evening, at the agency the party chose. Hosu is in every headline: on the night of the attack, creatures of the kind seen at the USJ tore through the city center, fires burned on its main street, and the reports say Endeavor and local pros brought it under control while Stain, the Hero Killer, was taken into custody. Footage of Stain standing before the arriving pros, and the words he shouted about false heroes, are everywhere online, and commentators tie the creatures to the League of Villains. That is all the public knows, unless the party was in Hosu itself and saw more.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the mentor calls the party in with a written evaluation for U.A. and reads it aloud. It is honest and specific: the first day's choices, the night patrol, the report, one real strength and one real fault, each with the moment that showed it. A party can argue a point; a good argument changes a line, a sulky one goes into the margin. If the week went well, the mentor offers a place for a work-study once the party holds a license; if it went badly, the evaluation says why without cruelty. The staff say goodbye, the costume goes back in its case, and the envelope is sealed for the homeroom teacher.

On the train back to U.A., the screens over the doors show Hosu on a loop, and passengers argue over what Stain said. The class chat compares evaluations: Kirishima proud of a single word of praise from Fourth Kind, Uraraka full of the capture moves Gunhead taught her, the chat stunned by the news and asking who was anywhere near Hosu.

By path: a 1-A party carries its envelope to Shota Aizawa. A 1-B party carries it to Vlad King, and Itsuka Kendo and Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu are on the same platform, comparing grades.

The event is complete when the evaluation is read and the party is on the train home, or the party leaves the agency without it.

side_work_study_first_shift.title: Work-Study: First Shift
side_work_study_first_shift.beats:
A weekday in the fall, between classes. The party holds a provisional license and a work-study placement, won in the Hero Work-Study quest, at the agency that accepted it; the mentor is that pro, played as the record describes, or a working pro of the narration's making. U.A. has approved the missed classes on one condition: grades hold. The party leaves campus after homeroom with a make-up worksheet in the bag. Other classmates leave on their own trains: Eijiro Kirishima for Fat Gum's agency in Osaka beside Tamaki Amajiki, Ochaco Uraraka and Tsuyu Asui for Ryukyu's agency beside Nejire Hado, Izuku Midoriya for Sir Nighteye's agency, where Mirio Togata works.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: a licensed student is not an intern. The mentor hands over a radio, a sector of the beat and a sidekick partner, and expects the party to judge when to act. The day is ordinary agency work, the kind the agency handles every week: a patrol, a lost wallet, a shop owner's complaint. Then the case: a delivery truck has gone into a storefront two blocks from the party's position, the driver is pinned behind a jammed door, a gas line hisses, and the sidekick partner is on the far side of the block. The party is first on scene, with the authority to clear the street, use a Quirk to free the driver and hold the scene until the mentor arrives. Moving too slowly costs the driver; moving carelessly costs the building.

Afterward the mentor reviews it plainly: what the license allowed, what the party did with it, what the report needs. Then the clock: the train back, a quiz tomorrow, the make-up worksheet still blank.

By path: a 1-A party comes home to a lounge where the other work-study students compare first shifts without saying much. A 1-B party is one of its class's first on placement, and its classmates want every detail.

The event is complete when the case is closed and the shift report is filed, or the party misses the train back to U.A.

side_winter_work_study.title: Winter Work-Study
side_winter_work_study.beats:
Mid-December, daytime, wherever the party is as winter Hero Work-Studies begin after the remedial provisional licenses and the Paranormal Liberation Front's hidden founding. Shoto Todoroki has invited Izuku Midoriya and Katsuki Bakugo to join him at the Endeavor Hero Agency under the new Number One hero, Endeavor, with Burnin and the Flaming Sidekickers setting a blistering pace from the first morning.

Default course as pressure: on the opening patrol through the city streets, the villain Starservant and his cult disciples shatter glass across a major intersection to stage a prophetic rampage. Before the three students can close the distance, Endeavor blasts from zero to full speed with Flashfire Fist, taking down the fleeing villain before the interns even reach the corner. Minutes later, the Number Two hero Hawks lands at the scene, chatting breezily while handing Endeavor a copy of Destro's Meta Liberation War book with highlighted passages. (Narrator only, private between Hawks and Endeavor unless the party closely observes the handoff: Hawks is covertly warning Endeavor that a liberation army of over a hundred thousand will strike in four months.) Turning back to the three interns, Endeavor asks what each lacks for the winter: Shoto wants to master Flashfire, Izuku wants control when power surges and the ability to use Air Force smoothly in battle, and Katsuki wants to discover what he cannot yet do. Endeavor gives them all one assignment: beat him to a single villain this winter.

By path: a Class 1-A student on winter work-study either trains directly alongside Izuku, Katsuki, and Shoto under Endeavor and Burnin—chasing the Number One hero's ignition speed through the streets—or crosses paths with their patrol during the Starservant response from another agency's beat.

The event is complete when the Starservant scene is cleared, Hawks delivers the book, and Endeavor sets his speed challenge for the winter.

side_todoroki_dinner.title: The Todoroki Family Dinner
side_todoroki_dinner.beats:
Mid-December, evening, a few days into the winter work-study with Endeavor and the night before the Ending incident. Fuyumi Todoroki has invited Shoto Todoroki and his work-study partners, Izuku Midoriya and Katsuki Bakugo, to the Todoroki Estate for a home-cooked dinner, hoping an ordinary meal with Shoto's friends will bring the family to the same table.

Default course as pressure: in the Main House, Fuyumi serves mapo tofu, sashimi, and chawanmushi while Natsuo Todoroki sits stiffly across from Endeavor, who came home early at Fuyumi's request. Katsuki immediately complains that the food is not spicy enough, marches into the kitchen to fix the seasoning, and detects the frigid silence at the table before anyone explains it. Izuku eats nervously between Shoto and Katsuki, trying not to stare as Shoto calmly passes dishes and addresses Endeavor as "my old man." Halfway through the meal, Natsuo cannot stomach the pretense any longer: his voice tightens, he tells Endeavor directly that he still cannot forgive him for what happened to their mother Rei and their late brother Toya, puts down his chopsticks, excuses himself with an apology to Fuyumi and the guests, and walks out toward the Garden to leave for the night. Afterward, while Katsuki washes his own plate and yells at Izuku and Shoto to stop dawdling, Izuku tells Shoto quietly outside the room that he can tell Shoto is getting ready to forgive his father, even if he is not there yet, and Endeavor steps onto the porch to thank Fuyumi for trying.

By path: a Class 1-A student invited along with Shoto, Izuku, and Katsuki sits at the Todoroki table—helping Fuyumi keep the conversation afloat, backing Katsuki in the kitchen, or speaking with Natsuo before he walks out into the December cold, setting up the following evening's crisis.

The event is complete when Natsuo leaves the table, the dishes are cleared, and the students head back from the Todoroki Estate.

v_bar_after_usj.title: The Bar After the USJ
v_bar_after_usj.beats:
A night in the days after the USJ attack, at the League Hideout Bar in Kamino Ward. Tomura Shigaraki sits on the end stool at the Bar Counter with bandages around his arms and legs where Snipe's bullets went through, scratching at his neck until it bleeds, while Kurogiri changes the dressings. A phone face-down on the counter keeps playing the news: an attack on U.A. Academy's students, dozens of thugs in custody, the huge black-skinned creature hauled away by police, All Might unhurt. The League is two people again.

Default course, as pressure the party can change: Tomura rants in game terms about cheats, about a boss stronger than the intel promised, about hired help who folded at the first hero. Anyone within reach is a target; he flexes his fingers at whoever speaks out of turn, and Kurogiri moves between them before a hand closes. Then the dark monitor on the back wall clicks and Sensei's voice fills the room, deep and warm. He is not angry. He asks Tomura what he learned, calls the loss of the Nomu an acceptable price for a lesson, and says the next game needs better players: people who choose this road for their own reasons, not for a day's wage. Then he asks whether anyone in the room is such a person. A good answer, a bold one or a lie that rings false is noticed. Tomura hates being lectured in front of hired help, and he remembers who saw it.

If the party went through Kurogiri's gate at the USJ, Tomura lumps it in with the rest, and police now hold thugs who saw its face; detectives will be asking around, and staying off the streets for a while cools that. If it was hired after the attack, it is the first new face Kurogiri has brought in, and Tomura insults it to see whether it flinches. Kurogiri pays exactly what was promised and asks quietly whether the party will stay.

The event is complete when the monitor goes dark and Tomura has decided whether the party is trash to throw out or a player worth keeping.

v_hired_muscle.title: Hired Muscle
v_hired_muscle.beats:
An evening in Kamino Ward a few days before the U.A. Sports Festival, with festival previews on every diner screen. A moneylender who works from an office above a pachinko parlor on the Shopping Street, a soft-spoken man in a cardigan with a ledger and no patience, has three accounts overdue and a fee for anyone who brings back cash tonight. Word reaches the party through a broker's text or a regular on Snack Bar Row; the meeting is a booth at the Late-Night Diner, across the road from the police box. He sends his own enforcer along, a heavy man who enjoys the work. The lender, his enforcer and everyone on his books are generated people.

Default course, as pressure the party can change: the first debtor is a day laborer in the Backstreets whose Quirk hardens his fists to stone; cornered, he swings, and a fight in a narrow lane brings neighbors to their windows with phones out. The second runs a noodle stall and shares a room with his younger sister, a grown woman working night shifts to pay his debt; she stands in the doorway and will not move, and the enforcer reaches for her first. The third is a mama on Snack Bar Row who pays in coins, smiles, and mentions that her cousin is a police sergeant in the next ward; leaning hard on her is the fastest way to put the police on the party's trail.

The party chooses how hard to lean: a threat, a broken shutter, a beating, a deal that buys a week, a debt quietly covered from its own pocket, or turning on the lender and his ledger. Any visit that ends in blood or a police report draws attention, the third most of all; clean collections, a name for being reasonable and a few quiet nights away from Kamino cool it. The enforcer reports everything, the lender pays in full only for cash, and his other clients hear how the party works. Violence stays quick and grounded and is never lingered over.

The event is complete when the three visits are done and the party has taken its fee, refused it or crossed the lender.

v_rooftop_rounds.title: Rooftop Rounds
v_rooftop_rounds.beats:
Late evening and night in Musutafu, a week or so after the USJ attack. The news still loops footage of the dome, pros are stretched thin, and the party is out in costume on its first real rounds: rooftops above the Musutafu Station District, the Station Concourse below, Izakaya Lane and the Back Alleys behind the arcade. Nobody hired it, nobody pays it and nobody licensed it.

Default course over one or two nights, as pressure the party can change. First, a purse snatcher on a bicycle tears a bag from an office worker at the Convenience Store Corner and races for the alleys; catching him is easy, deciding what to do with him is not, because holding a man for the police is itself an unlicensed arrest. Second, a drunk salaryman thrown out of a bar on Izakaya Lane has a Quirk that throws off bursts of static; he is shorting the signs and frightening the crowd, talking him down works as well as force, and force on a frightened drunk looks very different on a phone video. Third, after the trouble is over, a pro arrives late: Death Arms, out of breath from another call across town, looks at the tied-up thief or the calmed drunk and asks who called it in and who did the work. He has nothing against help, but help without a license is a crime and he says so bluntly. He wants a name, and the officer from the station police box wants a description of the costume for the log.

The party chooses: hand over the culprit and talk, slip away before the pro arrives, or stay and argue. Every sighting goes in the police log. Staying on camera, fighting in front of crowds and speaking for the costume draw attention to the mask; leaving no trace and resting the costume for a few nights cool it. People who were helped remember the mask kindly and say so to anyone who asks, police included.

The event is complete when the night's last call is handled and the party has faced the pro or vanished over the rooftops.

v_new_recruits.title: New Faces at the Bar
v_new_recruits.beats:
An evening at the League Hideout Bar, days after the Hosu incident. Every channel replays Stain, the Hero Killer, bleeding and standing before the pros, and the news ties the League of Villains to the Nomu loosed on Hosu that night. For the first time people want in, and Tomura Shigaraki hates that they come for Stain and not for him. He sits on the end stool at the Bar Counter; Kurogiri polishes glasses; the party is already there.

The slot at the Alley Entrance opens and Giran, the broker, comes in smiling with two introductions. Himiko Toga bounces in after him, gives her name brightly, says she wants to be Stain, or maybe to kill him, and asks to join. Dabi leans in the doorway, gives no name but Dabi, and asks whether the sulking man at the counter is really the one carrying on what Stain started.

Default course, as pressure the party can change: the newcomers needle Tomura, Tomura sneers back, and within minutes it breaks. Tomura reaches for Dabi with five fingers, blue fire wakes in Dabi's palm, Toga's knife comes out, and Kurogiri opens gates that swallow the reaching hands before anyone turns to dust or ash. Tomura walks out into the alley without a word. Hours later Tomura comes back calmer and colder: he has decided what he wants to break, and the newcomers can stay if they help him break it.

The party is in the room for all of it. It can step between them, back one side, make a friend of Toga (cheerful, unnerving and very interested in anyone who bleeds), get nothing from Dabi but a shrug, or stay out of the way. Whoever it sides with remembers, Tomura most of all. Before he leaves, Giran mentions one more candidate for another night: a gecko-faced admirer of Stain with a blade of strapped knives. This is the night the newcomers arrive, not the vetting work Kurogiri may hand out later. Dabi gives no past, and the scene invents none.

The event is complete when Tomura returns with his decision or the night ends with the newcomers gone.

v_tsukauchi_questions.title: A Detective's Questions
v_tsukauchi_questions.beats:
A weekday in early summer, during the day or early evening, weeks after the Hosu incident, with the police logging every masked figure on a roof. Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi of Musutafu Police Headquarters is following up reports that match the party: a costume, a Quirk, a route, a time of night. His partner, Officer Sansa Tamakawa, carries the folder. Tsukauchi's Quirk tells him whenever someone lies to him; he is courteous, exact and in no hurry.

How close he is depends on how much attention the party has drawn. If it has kept quiet, this is a canvass: the two officers knock on doors around the party's room or day job, show a blurred still from a security camera, and ask the party, along with the neighbors, whether it saw anything on certain nights. If its notoriety is growing, Tsukauchi asks for it by its cover name and invites it to a voluntary talk in the Detectives' Office, coffee on the table and the door open. If it is already wanted, he comes in person with a warning: he cannot arrest on a feeling, but he knows, and the next report ends in handcuffs or a pro at the door.

Default course, as pressure the party can change: his questions are short and he lets silence work. A flat lie is caught at once; he says so politely and writes it down. Silence, a refusal, a lawyer, careful true statements and questions back at him all work, and his questions show a sharp party what the police actually have. Leaving is allowed; running is noticed. Getting through clean and staying out of sight for a while cools things; a lie, a threat or a Quirk used near him heats them.

A vigilante hears that saving lives matters to him and still does not change the law; he says a license is the legal road and he would rather not make the arrest. An independent villain hears about the specific crime he is tracing and gets his card, and an offer to talk before the heroes find it.

The event is complete when Tsukauchi closes his notebook and the party knows roughly how close he is.

v_heist.title: The Armored Car Job
v_heist.beats:
Early summer in Kamino Ward, between first light and evening. An armored car carries the takings of a chain of pachinko parlors along the elevated ring road that loops the ward's industrial lots, and a crew means to take it. The guards, drivers, crew and inside man are generated people.

The job is today and the plan is already made: the party is picked up in a stolen van an hour before the hit and hears it once on the way (the minute the car slows at a ramp, masks, and the inside man, a young guard with gambling debts who will leave the rear door unlocked). The planner wants the party for what its Quirk can do; the take is split by shares. The hit happens in this scene and is never moved to another day: no tryouts, no rehearsal, no "come back later".

Default course, as pressure the party can change: the hit goes almost to plan. The van blocks the ramp, the rear door opens, the cases come out. Then the inside man panics, a second guard with skin-hardening fights back, a passing driver films everything and sirens start within minutes. Too early, Rock Lock, a local pro, arrives from a nearby call, touches the van and locks it in place. Getting away means leaving the van, the cases or a crew member behind. Rock Lock is not killed or crippled; he holds the scene for the police.

An independent villain came through a broker's introduction, owes the broker a cut and has nobody to call if it goes wrong. A League of Villains recruit was sent by Kurogiri because Giran's fees are due; Kurogiri opens a gate at an agreed spot after the job, never in sight of a hero or a police car.

This job draws attention no matter what. Masks, a clean exit and nobody hurt keep it a robbery the police file away; hurting the guards, a fight with Rock Lock on camera or a crew member caught alive puts the party's description in every briefing. Lying low after the split cools it.

The event is complete when the crew escapes with the cases, loses them or is caught, and the take is split or gone.

v_vanguard_briefing.title: The Vanguard Action Squad
v_vanguard_briefing.beats:
A late-July night at the League Hideout Bar, a week before U.A. Academy's Hero Course leaves for summer camp. The raid is set for the evening of Saturday, August 3, the camp's third night. The bar has never been this full. Tomura Shigaraki sits on the end stool; Kurogiri has cleared the Bar Counter for a hand-drawn map of a forested mountain: a lodge, trails, a cliff, the roads. Dabi leans bored by the door, Himiko Toga swings her legs, Spinner grips his blade of knives, Twice argues with himself, Mr. Compress rolls a marble across his knuckles, Magne rests her wrapped weapon on her knees, and as the briefing opens Kurogiri's gate brings in the three newcomers Sensei provided, each called by name from the moment he steps through: Mustard, Muscular and Moonfish. Where the League got its information is never explained.

Tomura names the Vanguard Action Squad and its target: Katsuki Bakugo, the Sports Festival winner who was chained snarling to the podium. The League's stated aim is to bring him in as a recruit. Default course, as pressure the party can change: Kurogiri lays out the roles (fire to cut the woods, gas on the trails, a team to hold the pros at the lodge, a hand to collect the target), Dabi gets the field and the signal to pull out, and the squad argues. Muscular wants the strongest opponent and nothing else; Spinner bristles that this is not what Stain stood for; Toga asks whether she may play with the cute ones; Mr. Compress promises a show; Twice cheers and boos in one breath; Magne tells them all to shut up and listen.
