The party can run a drill, test a pairing, take Monoma's side or Kendo's, or find a third plan both will accept. Kendo will keep working until the lights go off unless someone sends her to bed. In the evening the scene moves to the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge, where the class quizzes each other on hero law and the rules for using a Quirk in an emergency.

The event is complete when the class agrees on how it will move on exam day and Kendo calls it a night, or the party leaves.

b1_festival_rivalry.title: The Cultural Festival Rivalry
b1_festival_rivalry.beats:
The days before the School Festival at U.A. Academy. Class 1-B rehearses its stage play, "Romeo and Juliet and the Prisoner of Azkaban: The Return of the King," in costume on the Main Gymnasium stage: a tragedy, a prison break and a coronation folded into one script, which Neito Monoma insists will crush Class 1-A's band.

The cast in costume: Monoma as Romeo, in a doublet and cape; Yui Kodai as Juliet, in a long gown, who also uses her Quirk to grow and shrink the props between scenes; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu as Count Paris, the hooded villain whose last-act secret is that he is Romeo's father; Nirengeki Shoda and Yosetsu Awase as Romeo's men, whom Romeo shields in the tower duel. Itsuka Kendo keeps the rehearsal on schedule from the wings in her uniform, and the rest of the class runs the lights, the sets and the effects.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the rehearsal runs long. Monoma will not cut a line of Romeo's monologues, though the festival gives each class a strict time slot. Tetsutetsu keeps throwing back his hood before the reveal. Kodai's prop changes are perfect and silent, and nobody thanks her. Drums from Class 1-A's band practice carry across campus, and Monoma counts every missed beat aloud. Kendo wants one clean run before dark.

The party can take a small part, help backstage, cut the script, mend a costume, calm Monoma or fire him up, or help Kendo get a full run inside the time limit. A party at the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge finds the costume team sewing late into the evening.

The event is complete when the cast finishes one full run within the time slot, or the party leaves.

b1_hot_pot.title: 1-B Hot Pot Night
b1_hot_pot.beats:
A cold evening in mid-December at U.A. Academy. Class 1-B has pooled its money for a hot pot night, and the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge smells of broth from the Dorm Kitchen, where Itsuka Kendo runs the pot with a ladle and a timetable: vegetables first, then tofu, then the meat, in that order, no exceptions. Two burners sit on the low tables, and the class crowds around them on cushions.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: before anyone eats, Ibara Shiozaki asks for a moment of quiet and says grace; the class waits, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu with his chopsticks already raised. Then the meat goes in and the war begins. Tetsutetsu and Togaru Kamakiri reach for the same slice of beef every time, Tetsutetsu arguing that he needs the iron, Kamakiri arguing that he was faster. Kendo enforces a rotation. Neito Monoma critiques the broth, the cut of the meat, the dipping sauce and the seating plan, and somehow eats more than anyone. Hiryu Rin quietly adds a spice from home that makes half the table sweat and the other half ask for more. Kinoko Komori offers mushrooms, and Kendo checks that they came from a store. Pony Tsunotori, at her first proper hot pot, learns the word for the rice porridge made from the last of the broth and repeats it aloud until she has it. Vlad King looks in, is pressed to stay, and eats a bowl standing up.

The party can cook, guard the meat, take Monoma's critique seriously, or notice that Kendo has not sat down all evening and take over the ladle so she can. Whether she lets someone else run the pot is the small stake of the night.

The event is complete when the last of the broth has become porridge and the class cleans up together, or the party leaves.

b1_after_joint_training.title: After the Joint Training
b1_after_joint_training.beats:
An evening in the days after the Joint Training, in the Class 1-B Dorm Lounge at U.A. Academy. The five rounds at Training Ground Gamma are over and their results stand as this story decided them; nobody replays them here, they argue about them. Momo Yaoyorozu has come over from next door with her notebook, Eijiro Kirishima with a bag of snacks for Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, and Itsuka Kendo has cleared the low table for a proper debrief: what worked, what failed, what each class learned about the other.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Kendo and Yaoyorozu compare plans and find they made the same mistake from opposite sides; they write it down. Juzo Honenuki adds one quiet correction to each of their notes. Tetsutetsu and Kirishima argue over who took the harder hits and agree it was both. Ibara Shiozaki asks forgiveness of everyone she bound. Neito Monoma stands on a chair and demands a rematch, all five rounds, this week, and asks the 1-A guests with exquisite courtesy how it feels to need help from General Studies, forgetting that 1-B had Hitoshi Shinso on its side too. The talk turns to Shinso: the teachers gave their verdict at the end of the day, by canon default that he is on track to join the Hero Course next spring, and even Monoma admits through his teeth that the capture scarf was well used. Katsuki Bakugo, off at his work-study by default, is a topic of the debrief but not in the room.

By path: a 1-B party is a host and can lead the debrief, back Monoma's rematch, or tell him what he did well in his round, which leaves him speechless. A 1-A party is a guest in rival territory: Monoma will needle, Tetsutetsu will offer a drink and a challenge, and an honest word of credit for 1-B's plans earns Kendo's respect.

The event is complete when the notes are traded and Vlad King looks in to send the 1-A guests home, or the party leaves.

side_full_cowl.title: Full Cowl
side_full_cowl.beats:
Late April, daytime, during the Hero Agency Internship week at Gran Torino's Apartment. The cramped Main Room is littered with laundry and boxes, and the retired pro Sorahiko Torino plays the doddering old man, asking Izuku Midoriya who he is before dropping the act mid-sentence and ricocheting off the walls, floor and ceiling with Jet faster than the eye can track.

Default course as pressure: Gran Torino batters Izuku across the room to show him why his fighting failed at the Sports Festival. Izuku treats One For All as a special trump card he switches on in a single limb when he is desperate, instead of part of his own body, and his admiration for All Might keeps his movements stiff. The lesson pauses only when the microwave dings in Gran Torino's Kitchenette. The old man pulls out a plate of taiyaki that is scorching outside and still icy in the center because the turntable was jammed. Looking at the unevenly heated fish pastry gives Izuku the answer: instead of focusing power into one point after he moves, he must circulate a low, even five percent through his whole body from the start. By the final bouts he holds One For All: Full Cowl across the room, trading high-speed rebounds with his mentor and landing a grazing blow before Gran Torino puts him on the floorboards again.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student interning at Gran Torino's Apartment or visiting on a joint patrol drill is thrown straight into the same close-quarters gauntlet. Gran Torino calls both young people "kid," bounces off the walls to test their reflexes from blind angles, and forces the party to keep its Quirk active and controlled on the move rather than saving one big swing.

The event is complete when Izuku holds Full Cowl at five percent through a three-minute spar in the apartment and Gran Torino sits down to finish his warm taiyaki.

v_stain_meets_league.title: The Hero Killer at the Bar
v_stain_meets_league.beats:
Late April, evening to late night at the League Hideout Bar, days before the Hosu incident. The broker Giran brings a prospective ally through the Alley Entrance to the Bar Counter: Stain, the Hero Killer, bandage-wrapped and armed with knives and a katana. Kurogiri polishes glasses behind the bar while Tomura Shigaraki slouches on a stool with the severed hand he calls Father over his face.

Default course as pressure: Kurogiri hopes to recruit the notorious killer, and Shigaraki expects an easy alliance between men who destroy heroes. Instead, the talk sours within minutes. Shigaraki brags about smashing everything that annoys him, starting with All Might and the U.A. Academy brats from the USJ. Stain answers with a low, rasping "Hah..." and judges Shigaraki a brat throwing a tantrum without conviction. When Shigaraki reaches out to decay him, Stain vaults the counter, pins him to the floorboards with a blade at his throat, cuts his shoulder, and paralyzes both Shigaraki and Kurogiri with Bloodcurdle. Only when Shigaraki, bleeding and clawing at his neck, forces out that he wants to ruin a society that worships All Might does Stain sheathe his knife. Calling it a seed of conviction worth watching, Stain demands that Kurogiri warp him back to Hosu to finish his own purge.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit is in the bar when Giran arrives and faces Stain's measure firsthand. The recruit can step between the Hero Killer and Shigaraki, cross blades to test Stain's speed, or answer Stain's demand for a creed before Kurogiri talks the room down; Stain spares no one who fights for petty spite alone, but stays his hand if the recruit forces a standoff or speaks with real purpose.

The event is complete when Stain judges the League's answer and steps through Kurogiri's warp gate back to Hosu.

side_kamino_reckoning.title: The Rebuke
side_kamino_reckoning.beats:
Early August, evening, outside Heights Alliance in the Heights Alliance Yard at U.A. Academy. The crisis in Kamino Ward is over, All Might has retired, and Class 1-A has been called out before dinner to face Shota Aizawa under the courtyard lights. The air between the five students who went to Kamino and the classmates who stayed behind is strained and quiet.

Default course as pressure: Aizawa addresses the class in his flat, low voice. He tells Izuku Midoriya, Tenya Iida, Shoto Todoroki, Eijiro Kirishima, and Momo Yaoyorozu that breaking rules to play vigilante in Kamino shattered the faculty's trust, and tells everyone else who knew of their plan and said nothing—everyone except Katsuki Bakugo, Kyoka Jiro and Toru Hagakure, who were hurt or unconscious that night—that they share the blame. If U.A. Academy were not under emergency campus lockdown after All Might's retirement, he would expel every one of them except those three on the spot; instead, he orders them to rebuild their trust strictly by the book and walks inside. In the awkward silence, Tsuyu Asui finally speaks up, tears spilling down her face: she tells the five how hurt and frightened she was that they went into danger after she warned them, and how badly she wants them all to be friends again without breaking the rules. The rescuers apologize in full, hugging her in the yard. Meanwhile, Katsuki Bakugo grabs Denki Kaminari, drags him behind the bushes to force him into his short-circuited "Wheey" state so the class laughs, and shoves an envelope of cash into Kirishima's chest to repay the night-vision goggles Kirishima bought to save him.

By path: a Class 1-A student stands in the yard for Aizawa's judgment—counted among those who went, those who stayed silent, or the few who spoke against it—and helps mend the rift with Tsu and the others in the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge afterward.

The event is complete when Tsuyu's tears dry, Bakugo pays his debt, and Class 1-A heads into the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge together.

side_big_three.title: The Big Three
side_big_three.beats:
Mid-September, daytime at U.A. Academy, at the start of the second term. To explain the Hero Work-Studies that go beyond first-term internships, Shota Aizawa brings the academy's top three third-year students—the Big Three—into Class 1-A Homeroom: Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, and Nejire Hado.

Default course as pressure: the introduction starts oddly. Tamaki stares intensely at the class to picture them as potatoes, then gives up, turns to face the homeroom wall, and mutters that he wants to go home. Nejire immediately darts from desk to desk firing rapid-fire questions about Mina Ashido's horns, Shoto Todoroki's burn scar, and everyone else's Quirks before anyone can answer. Mirio opens with a flat pun that lands on dead silence, laughs loudly anyway, and proposes moving to the Main Gymnasium so the first-years can learn by fighting him all at once. On the gym floor, Mirio's clothes drop as his Quirk activates, he apologizes mid-slip, and within seconds he sinks through the floor with Permeation to take out the long-range attackers first before dropping the close-range fighters with single precision body blows. Even when Izuku Midoriya reads his resurface angle, Mirio slips the counter through sheer prediction. Afterward, fully dressed again, Mirio explains that Permeation leaves him blind, deaf, and breathless underground; what beat Class 1-A was not a flashy power, but the experience and foresight he gained on work-study under Sir Nighteye. It is a supervised bout where no student is badly hurt.

By path: a Class 1-A student faces Mirio on the Main Gymnasium floor alongside the class and tests a plan against his prediction; a Class 1-B student observing from the Main Building Hallway or joining the joint session gets the chance to step onto the mat and test 1-B's teamwork against Lemillion.

The event is complete when Mirio finishes the bout, explains how work-study built his skill, and the Big Three take questions from the first-years.

side_nighteye_stamp.title: Nighteye's Stamp Test
side_nighteye_stamp.beats:
Late September, daytime at the Sir Nighteye Hero Agency. Mirio Togata brings Izuku Midoriya into the Agency Office to apply for a Hero Work-Study under All Might's former sidekick, Sir Nighteye. The office walls are lined with rare All Might posters and memorabilia, Centipeder works quietly in the Meeting Room, and Nighteye's doctrine that an agency must run on humor is enforced on the spot as Bubble Girl struggles through a flat joke.

Default course as pressure: Izuku tries to meet the humor rule by contorting his face into an All Might impression. It fails miserably; Nighteye stares at him through rectangular glasses with cold severity because the impression wrinkles a detail of All Might's brow wrong. Nighteye states bluntly that Mirio Togata should have been chosen as All Might's successor, not Izuku, and refuses to sign Izuku's work-study contract automatically. Instead, he holds up his official agency seal and gives a three-minute test: if Izuku wants the stamp on his form, he must take the seal from Nighteye's hand and stamp the paper himself while Mirio steps outside. With one use of Foresight, Nighteye slips every Full Cowl rush, hurling heavy five-kilogram seals to pin Izuku back while pressing him on why All Might chose him. Izuku still cannot touch Nighteye before the three minutes expire, but as he rebounds off the walls, he takes extra care never to step on a single All Might poster on the floor. Seeing that devotion—and wanting to show Izuku the realities of the street—Nighteye takes the form and stamps it himself.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student who comes with Mirio and Izuku to apply at the Sir Nighteye Hero Agency must first attempt a joke to satisfy Nighteye's humor requirement, then either join the three-minute stamp test in the Agency Office or run an observation drill with Centipeder and Bubble Girl to earn Nighteye's signature.

The event is complete when the three-minute test ends and Sir Nighteye stamps the work-study paperwork.

side_fat_gum_patrol.title: Unbreakable
side_fat_gum_patrol.beats:
Early October, daytime in Osaka Downtown and the Fat Gum Hero Agency. The BMI Hero Fat Gum walks a lively street patrol through the Covered Arcade and Dotonbori Canal with his third-year intern Tamaki Amajiki and his new Class 1-A work-study student Eijiro Kirishima, chatting with shopkeepers and sharing takoyaki between street checks.

Default course as pressure: a street gang fight breaks out in the Covered Arcade and spills into the Back Streets. Fat Gum sinks the fleeing thugs straight into his body, and Tamaki pins the rest with clam shells and octopus tentacles, until a panicked gunman in the crowd fires a strange dart from the shadows. The round hits Tamaki in the arm; when he tries to manifest his Quirk again, nothing happens—his power has been temporarily erased. Before the shooter can escape, a cornered confederate injects himself with the black-market drug Trigger, sprouting long blades from his body that slice through Eijiro's ordinary Hardening and threaten bystanders in the alley. Remembering how he froze in the past, Eijiro refuses to back down and pushes his Quirk beyond its normal limit, hardening every inch of his skin, teeth, and eyes into jagged armor: Red Riot Unbreakable. He shatters the Trigger-boosted blades, drives the villain back into Fat Gum's waiting belly, and secures the arrest. Afterward, at the Fat Gum Agency Front Office, Tamaki's Quirk begins to return after rest, and Fat Gum bags the crushed dart casing as hard evidence of a Quirk-destroying drug on the streets.

By path: a Class 1-A or Class 1-B student on work-study patrols beside Kirishima and Tamaki; a Licensed Pro Hero or Licensed Sidekick working the Osaka beat joins Fat Gum's pursuit in the Back Streets, helps shield civilians from the Trigger blades, or tracks the shooter who fired the dart.

The event is complete when the Trigger-boosted villain is in Fat Gum's custody, Tamaki is checked over, and the bullet evidence is secured.

side_eri_visit.title: A Smile for Eri
side_eri_visit.beats:
Late October, daytime in the Patient Rooms of Musutafu General Hospital, a week after the Shie Hassaikai raid. The fever from Eri's horn has subsided, and Shota Aizawa stands near the door as her guardian so he can erase her Quirk if it stirs. Izuku Midoriya and Mirio Togata arrive with a basket of fruit to see her for the first time since the rescue.

Default course as pressure: Eri sits propped up in the hospital bed, small and quiet, apologizing before anyone asks a question. She thanks Izuku and Mirio for saving her and asks after everyone who was hurt, blaming herself because she still does not know what her power does or why people bled for her. Even when Mirio makes a goofy face and peels an apple into slices for her, her expression remains still; the shadow of Kai Chisaki lingers, and she does not know how to smile. Remembering that U.A. Academy is preparing its autumn School Festival, Izuku and Mirio ask Aizawa's permission and invite Eri to come see the festival—a day of music, dancing, and sweet stalls—promising that if she comes, they will help her find a real smile. Eri does not understand what a festival is, so she asks politely to hear more, and Aizawa agrees to arrange a brief, supervised preview walk of U.A. Academy before the crowds arrive so the child will not be overwhelmed on the day. The scene stays gentle and child-safe throughout.

By path: a Class 1-A student visiting the Patient Rooms with Izuku helps put Eri at ease at her level—talking quietly about campus life, peeling fruit, or promising what Class 1-A will build for the festival—without crowding or frightening her.

The event is complete when Eri accepts the invitation to the School Festival and Aizawa approves her supervised campus visit.

side_festival_rehearsal.title: The Band
side_festival_rehearsal.beats:
Late October to early November, evenings at U.A. Academy in the final week before the School Festival. In the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge, Tenya Iida and Momo Yaoyorozu lead a vote to choose Class 1-A's festival event—something that will lift the spirit of the whole campus, other courses included, after months of tension.

Default course as pressure: the class settles on a live concert with a dance performance and stage effects, and everyone looks straight at Kyoka Jiro. She turns red, twists her earlobe jacks, and tries to deflect, until Denki Kaminari and Eijiro Kirishima remind her how much her music means to her; she agrees to lead the band and sing. Auditions in the Music Room quickly sort the players: Katsuki Bakugo blasts the drum kit with explosive precision after refusing at first and swearing they will crush every listener in the hall, Momo takes the keyboard, Kaminari and Tokoyami take guitars, and Jiro takes bass and vocals. In the lounge, Mina Ashido drills the dancers—Izuku Midoriya, Ochaco Uraraka, Tenya Iida, and the rest—while Shoto Todoroki, Eijiro Kirishima, and Yuga Aoyama plan an ice-and-light disco ball for the gym ceiling. Meanwhile, training outside in the Heights Alliance Yard before dusk, Izuku works on long-range wind pressure and visits Mei Hatsume in the Development Studio, where she enthusiastically outfits him with her newest "baby": support gloves that focus twenty-percent finger flicks into clean Air Force blasts.

By path: a Class 1-A student takes a role in the band, the dance crew, or the stage-effects team across the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge and Music Room, or tests gear alongside Izuku and Hatsume in the Development Studio.

The event is complete when the band's arrangement locks in, the dance and stage cues are set, and Izuku tests his Air Force gloves.

v_gigantomachia_trials.title: The Giant
v_gigantomachia_trials.beats:
Throughout November, day and night, wherever the League of Villains is camped in the wilderness before the Battle of Deika. After All For One's bodyguard Gigantomachia rejected Tomura Shigaraki as too weak to succeed his master, Dr. Kyudai Garaki gave the League one condition for his backing and resources: bend the giant to Shigaraki's will in combat.

Default course as pressure: for weeks on end, the League fights Gigantomachia across rugged ravines and mountain slopes. Every forty-eight hours and forty-four minutes, the giant stops only for three hours of sleep before waking to hunt Shigaraki all over again. Dabi's blue flames scorch the rock without slowing him, Himiko Toga and Spinner dart from cover to buy seconds, Twice makes doubles to pull the bruised out of reach, and Mr. Compress pockets boulders and exhausted comrades alike, yet Gigantomachia tears through hillsides roaring for his master. Exhausted and sleepless, Shigaraki refuses to retreat; his speed sharpens and his Decay begins spreading beyond the five fingers he touches directly. Just as Shigaraki swears he will tame the giant in the next waking cycle, word comes through the underworld: the Meta Liberation Army's leader, Re-Destro, holds the broker Giran captive in Deika City and challenges the League to come fight his army or watch their broker die.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit endures the grueling mountain attrition alongside Shigaraki, Dabi, Toga, Twice, Spinner, and Compress—taking shifts to bait Gigantomachia's charges, covering Shigaraki during the three-hour rest windows, and weighing in when Re-Destro's ultimatum over Giran arrives.

The event is complete when the League survives another waking bout with Gigantomachia and hears Re-Destro's challenge to march on Deika City.

v_hawks_joins.title: The Number Two
v_hawks_joins.beats:
Mid-December, evening to late night in the Yokohama Harbor District, after the Paranormal Liberation Front's founding and the start of Tomura Shigaraki's four-month procedure. Out on the Container Docks and near the Dockside Safehouse, Dabi meets the Wing Hero Hawks, Japan's Number Two pro hero, who has been courting the League since the Kyushu High-End attack.

Default course as pressure: Hawks lands with his usual breezy smile, hands in his flight jacket pockets, and asks to be brought into the inner circle now that the League and the Meta Liberation Army have merged. Dabi leans against a shipping container, low and sardonic, and refuses to trust a hero's words alone: if the Number Two wants a seat in the Front, he has to prove he has crossed the line in blood. When Hawks returns for the second meeting, he carries a heavy duffel bag onto the docks and unzips it at Dabi's feet to reveal what looks to be the corpse of the missing Number Three hero, Best Jeanist. (Narrator only, covert truth the recruit does not know: Best Jeanist is alive in suspended animation under the Commission's secret operation; on the docks, the recruit sees only what Dabi sees.) Dabi inspects the body in the bag with a flat smirk, remarks that Hawks really is crazy despite doubting whether it is truly Jeanist, and grants Hawks access as a lieutenant's contact while keeping him under quiet watch.

By path: a League of Villains Recruit accompanies Dabi to the Container Docks as backup, watches the perimeter for Hero Public Safety Commission tails, questions Hawks face-to-face when he hands over the bag, and decides whether to report concerns about the Wing Hero's true motives.

The event is complete when Hawks presents the duffel bag on the docks and Dabi accepts him into the Front's network on probation.

side_walk_home_deku.title: Walking Back with Iida and Uraraka
side_walk_home_deku.beats:
Monday, late afternoon at U.A. Academy, the first day of classes: the party is walking back across the grounds toward Heights Alliance with Izuku Midoriya and Ochaco Uraraka after the Quirk Apprehension Test. Izuku's swollen finger is freshly bandaged by Recovery Girl, and all of them are still recovering from Shota Aizawa's parting words: nobody is expelled, the threat was a logical ruse. Tenya Iida catches up at a brisk walk and falls into step, chopping the air.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Tenya admits, stiff with embarrassment, that he swallowed the ruse whole; it never crossed his mind that a U.A. teacher would lie to a class, and he cannot decide whether to be shocked or impressed. He asks about Izuku's finger and how a Quirk can hit that hard and break its owner; Izuku dodges with a nervous laugh and a mutter about control. Then Ochaco remembers the name Katsuki Bakugo yelled across the field and asks whether Izuku is called Deku. He explains that his name is Izuku and that Deku is Katsuki's insult for him: useless. Ochaco decides she likes it anyway, because to her ear it echoes 'dekiru', the word for being able to do a thing: a name that says 'can do!' Izuku goes scarlet to the ears and blurts that Deku is fine, while Tenya protests that an insult cannot possibly be fine.

The party has a real voice: tell the story of its own test, take Tenya's side or Ochaco's on the name, tease Izuku while he glows, suggest a nickname of its own, or simply walk along and listen. A player who placed near the bottom of the test gets honest relief from all three.

The event is complete when Ochaco has given 'Deku' its new meaning and the group reaches Heights Alliance, or the party splits off from them.

side_first_lessons.title: The First Ordinary Lessons
side_first_lessons.beats:
Tuesday morning at U.A. Academy, the first ordinary day of the timetable: the party is with classmates in its homeroom, and the famous Hero Course's core classes turn out to be plain school. Present Mic bounds in for English at full broadcast volume, calls the room his listeners, demands a big 'YEAH!' and gets near silence, then writes a dry grammar drill on the board: four sentences, one wrong relative pronoun, find it. Someone mutters that the most surprising thing at U.A. so far is how normal this is.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Present Mic calls on the party. The player can answer, get it wrong with style, give his call-and-response the volume he wants, or ask what grammar has to do with heroics (he has a loud answer about reports, interviews and overseas team-ups). At noon the class pours into Lunch Rush's Cafeteria. Lunch Rush serves first-rate rice, grilled fish, curry and soba at student prices, with a few courteous words from behind his mask, and the first bite silences the table. Talk turns to the afternoon: hero training, and nobody knows yet what it will be.

By path: Class 1-A has heard a famous teacher will take its afternoon lesson and speculates loudly. Class 1-B has its own English hour with Present Mic in the Class 1-B Homeroom, then its own afternoon of hero training, and its table trades notes with 1-A across the aisle. If the event opens at lunch, the morning's drill comes up as a story over trays, and Present Mic passes with his own tray and quizzes the table. The party can pick a table, share a dish, argue for the best thing on the menu or guess at the afternoon.

The event is complete when lunch is over and the class heads off to the afternoon's hero training, or the party leaves.

side_bakugo_gate.title: Bakugo at the Gate
side_bakugo_gate.beats:
Tuesday, late afternoon at U.A. Academy, after the Battle Trial: the party is out on the grounds near the Main Gate with Izuku Midoriya, his arm freshly bandaged by Recovery Girl, and Katsuki Bakugo, who walked out of class without a word and has stopped only because Izuku shouted 'Kacchan!' after him. By canon default Izuku's team beat Katsuki's today; if the trial went otherwise, Katsuki's fury fixes on whoever beat him or showed him up.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Izuku lowers his voice and half-confesses that his power was given to him by someone, that he cannot say more, and that he was never deceiving Katsuki all those years; one day he will make it his own and win with it. A player standing close hears only that much, never a name or a how, and asking later gets a stammer and a change of subject. Katsuki barely takes it in. Shaking, eyes wet with rage, he says today stands as a loss: he watched Shoto Todoroki's ice and knew he could not beat it, he heard Momo Yaoyorozu's analysis and agreed with every word. Then he swears to beat every one of them from here on and become Number One. All Might bounds up the path with a booming 'Young Bakugo!' to encourage him; Katsuki shrugs off the hand on his shoulder and says he will surpass All Might too.

The party can step back and leave the two of them the gate, stand at Izuku's side, push Katsuki and get snarled at, or offer him a word he throws back. A challenge from the player becomes part of the vow: Katsuki adds the player by name to the list of people he will beat. Once he stalks off, All Might thanks the party for being there, a little sheepishly.

The event is complete when Katsuki has made his vow and walked off, or the party leaves them.

side_aizawa_returns.title: Aizawa Returns in Bandages
side_aizawa_returns.beats:
Thursday morning at U.A. Academy, the first class day after the attack on the USJ: the party is with classmates, by canon default in the Class 1-A Homeroom before the bell, where Tenya Iida chops the air and orders everyone into their seats. The room is tense: the news still shows the dome, and nobody knows who will take homeroom.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the door slides open and Shota Aizawa shuffles in, wrapped in bandages from scalp to elbows, both arms in casts, only his eyes and hair showing. The class shouts his name, and Tenya asks whether he should even be standing. Aizawa says his health is irrelevant and that the fight is not over. The room braces for more villains, and he announces the U.A. Sports Festival in two weeks. Relief turns into a roar, then into doubt: Minoru Mineta and others ask whether a festival right after a villain attack is wise. Aizawa answers flatly that security will be stronger than ever and that the festival shows the school is not shaken. Every pro agency in the country scouts it and the whole nation watches; a student gets only three in a career, and anyone who wants to go pro cannot waste one.

If the party is elsewhere on campus with classmates when the morning starts, Aizawa finds the group on his way in and says the same in fewer words. The party can greet him, ask about Thirteen (stable and recovering, nothing more), ask what the festival will demand, or say what the USJ cost it. A player who fought at the USJ gets one long, silent look from him that passes for thanks.

The event is complete when the Sports Festival is announced and homeroom moves on to the day's lessons, or the party leaves.

side_uraraka_reason.title: Why Uraraka Wants to Be a Hero
side_uraraka_reason.beats:
Thursday, lunch hour at U.A. Academy, the day the Sports Festival was announced: the party is with Ochaco Uraraka on the way down to Lunch Rush's Cafeteria, and she is not her usual self. Since homeroom she has worn a fierce, set face that startles everyone, fists clenched, telling anyone near her to give the festival everything.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Izuku Midoriya and Tenya Iida catch up on the stairs, and Izuku finally asks why she wants to be a hero. Ochaco wilts, laughs, and admits it: money. Pressed, she explains without self-pity. Her parents run a small construction company that gets very little work. Years ago she offered to join them and float materials for free with her Quirk, and her father told her he would rather see her chase her own dream. So she will become a pro, earn well, and give her parents an easy life. Tenya declares it splendid at full volume. Izuku goes quiet: he had thought a hero working for money was a lesser thing, and he sees that hers is a reason built around other people. Both of them look at her differently for the rest of the day, and the attention flusters her.

The party has a part: share its own reason and see how hers sits beside it, praise her, tease her gently about money, or ask about the family company. Ochaco is grateful for honesty and embarrassed by fuss; she makes the party promise not to spread it around, then laughs at herself for asking. If the party is already at a table in the cafeteria, the same talk happens over trays.

The event is complete when Ochaco has told her reason and the group goes on to lunch, or the party leaves.

side_all_might_lunch.title: Lunch with All Might
side_all_might_lunch.beats:
Thursday, lunch hour at U.A. Academy, the day the Sports Festival was announced: the party is with Izuku Midoriya in a corridor on the way to lunch when All Might fills the passage. He holds out a lunch box that looks tiny in his enormous hands and, swaying shyly, asks in a coy little voice whether Young Midoriya would care to have lunch with him.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Ochaco Uraraka, beside them or passing by, dissolves into helpless laughter and cannot stop; Izuku is mortified, then thrilled. All Might, back at full volume, steers him off toward the Teachers' Lounge. The party can laugh along, ask to come too (All Might apologizes warmly: this is a teacher's talk with one student, and he promises the party its own turn another day), tease Izuku about being the favorite, or walk them to the lounge door. The door closes and the narration stays outside: what is said in there is private between All Might and Izuku.

When Izuku comes out he is lit up with resolve and says only that All Might wants him to use the festival to show the whole country who he is, to stand up and tell the world he is here. Asked why All Might keeps picking him, Izuku stammers something about the entrance exam and changes the subject; pressing gets nothing more. Ochaco, still giggling, wants to know whether the tiny lunch box had a pattern on it.

The event is complete when Izuku has gone to lunch with All Might and come back fired up for the festival, or the party leaves.

side_door_crowd.title: The Crowd at Class 1-A's Door
side_door_crowd.beats:
Thursday, after the last bell at U.A. Academy, the day the Sports Festival was announced: the party is at the door of the Class 1-A Homeroom, or wherever Class 1-A is leaving from, and the way out is jammed. Students from General Studies, Support, Management and Class 1-B have come to look at the class that survived the villains, and nobody in 1-A can get past them.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: a 1-A classmate asks what is going on, and Minoru Mineta wails that he cannot get out. Katsuki Bakugo shoulders to the front, tells the crowd that scouting the competition is pointless and that they should move, extras. Tenya Iida scolds him for insulting the whole school. Hitoshi Shinso slips to the front, unhurried and tired-eyed, and says he expected more from the Hero Course. Calmly, he explains that festival results can move people from General Studies into the Hero Course, and the other way around; he did not come to look, he came to declare war. He does not use his Quirk here. From the back, Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu of Class 1-B bellows that he came to say something too: 1-A is getting cocky after one fight, they had better not embarrass the school, and 1-B is coming for them. Katsuki pushes through the crowd, says only first place counts, and leaves the rest of 1-A groaning that every course now hates them.

By path: a Class 1-A player is inside the room and can answer the crowd, back Katsuki, apologize for him or take Shinso's challenge personally. A General Studies player stands beside Shinso and can join the declaration, call it out or meet a 1-A student's eye. A Class 1-B player is at the back with Tetsutetsu and can add a challenge of its own or hold him back. Shinso remembers anyone who stands up to him.

The event is complete when the crowd breaks up and the challenges stand, or the party leaves.

side_shoto_mother.title: Shoto Visits His Mother
side_shoto_mother.beats:
Late April, on one of the two days off after the Sports Festival, wherever the party is with Shoto Todoroki: he has been quieter than usual since the festival, and today he says, without being asked, that he is going to see his mother. He has not seen her in years.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Shoto is heading for Musutafu General Hospital, where she has lived in a private room for a long time. He says he has to talk with her before he can face his own power and become the hero he wants to be, one of his own choosing. He explains no more than he has already told the party; the rest is his. If the player offers to come, he thinks it over and allows only as far as he can bear: the hospital entrance, the lobby, or the corridor outside her door. He goes in alone, and the narration stays outside with the party. After a long while he comes out with red-rimmed eyes and a face the party has not seen on him before. He says only that she cried, that she apologized, that she welcomed him and even smiled, and that he will come back.

The party can walk with him in silence, wait outside without a single question, buy him a drink from the vending machine after, or decide this is not its place and let him go alone, which he thanks the party for. Pressing for details shuts him down; patience earns one more sentence later, about the All Might videos his mother once watched with him. If the festival went differently and Shoto never faced his fire there, he still goes: something at the festival made him think of her, and that is enough.

The event is complete when Shoto has seen his mother and left the hospital, or he heads off alone and the party lets him go.

side_tokoyami_hawks.title: Tokoyami at Hawks's Agency
side_tokoyami_hawks.beats:
Internship week, at the turn of April into May, at Hawks Hero Agency in Fukuoka: the party is with Fumikage Tokoyami, who took Hawks's offer and is still waiting to be shown anything. Hawks drifts in, wings folded, coffee in hand, and says they might as well come along.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: a call comes in and Hawks is gone before anyone stands. By the time Tokoyami and the party reach the street, the purse snatcher is pinned under a feather, the crash victims are sitting on the curb, and Hawks is chatting with a police officer. It happens three times before lunch. His sidekicks arrive after him every time, carry the paperwork and the cleanup, and none of them seems surprised. Hawks is friendly, quick and impossible to pin down: heroes should be so fast they have free time, he says, and the slow ones should work on catching up. Over lunch he asks Tokoyami, casually, about the USJ: how many villains, what the man covered in hands said, what the warp gate could do, whether anyone named who they answer to. Tokoyami tells what he knows while Dark Shadow chatters. Hawks never says why he asks. By evening Tokoyami says, low, that he has learned nothing here except how far behind he is.

By path: a Class 1-A intern runs beside Tokoyami and can try to keep up, ask Hawks for an actual lesson, or answer his questions about the USJ from its own memory; the narration never explains his interest. A Licensed Pro or Licensed Sidekick on a team-up with Hawks this week sees it from the staff side: the cleanup lands on the party, Hawks praises it in passing, and asking why he took an intern who cannot fly earns a grin and a joke.

The event is complete when the day's calls are done and Tokoyami has said what the week is teaching him, or the party leaves the agency.

side_ingenium_name.title: At Tensei's Bedside
side_ingenium_name.beats:
Late April, on one of the two days off after the Sports Festival, in the Hospital Ward of Hosu General Hospital: the party is with Tenya Iida outside the room of his older brother Tensei, the pro hero Ingenium, whom the Hero Killer struck down in Hosu on the day of the festival. Tenya left the festival for this bedside and has hardly slept.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Tensei lies bandaged in bed, but he smiles when Tenya comes in and teases him gently for the frown. Tenya may ask the party to wait in the corridor; Tensei, hearing a friend came along, asks to meet them, and the player can stay by the door or take the chair. Tensei says the doctors have told him plainly that his legs will not recover and his hero career is over. He apologizes for falling short as a big brother and tells Tenya he has always been a brilliant younger one. Then he asks Tenya to take on the name Ingenium and carry it forward. Tenya cannot answer. He grips the bed rail, says he needs time, and does not accept; the name stays unclaimed.

The party can comfort Tenya in the corridor, tell Tensei what his brother did at the festival, keep a respectful silence, or notice what Tenya keeps asking the nurses: which street it happened on, whether the man has been caught. He leaves with his jaw set and his voice far too even, and turns aside any offer of help with polite thanks.

If the story has already changed what happened to Tensei, the talk follows his real condition instead, and the name is only a hope for the future.

The event is complete when Tensei has asked Tenya to carry the name and Tenya has left the room without accepting it, or the party leaves.

side_back_from_internships.title: Back from Internships
side_back_from_internships.beats:
Early May, the first school day after Internship Week, wherever the player is on the grounds of U.A. Academy. The agency week is over and the classmates around the player are trading stories before lessons. Then Katsuki Bakugo walks in with his hair combed flat and parted in a prim, glossy eight-to-two line, the work of Best Jeanist, who spent the week correcting his manners and his look. Eijiro Kirishima takes one look and doubles over; Hanta Sero joins him until both are wheezing. Bakugo says it will not go back and that he will kill them both.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the stories go around. Ochaco Uraraka, back from Gunhead's agency, drops into a crisp martial-arts stance and breathes out slow and steady, and the people beside her step back. Minoru Mineta, back from Mount Lady, stares at nothing and announces that women are scary, which earns him no sympathy. Momo Yaoyorozu, a little embarrassed, explains that she and Itsuka Kendo of Class 1-B spent much of the week filming a commercial with Uwabami. Tsuyu Asui mentions in one sentence that she was out on a sea patrol with Selkie. Shoto Todoroki, asked about Hosu, keeps to the official story: Endeavor arrived and dealt with the Hero Killer, and says nothing more. The player can share their own week, tease Bakugo, defend him, or keep the Hosu story straight.

Before the bell the laughter goes one beat too far: Bakugo's temper flares, a small blast pops off his scalp, and the neat part springs back into its usual spikes in a puff of smoke. Kirishima calls it a relief; Bakugo calls him something worse.

By path: a Class 1-A student is in the thick of it. A Class 1-B student catches it from the corridor or with Kendo, who tells the commercial from her side and admits the camera crew was harder on her than any drill, while Neito Monoma sniffs at all the attention 1-A gets.

The event is complete when Bakugo's hair has blown back into spikes and the lessons begin, or the party leaves.

side_peephole.title: The Peephole
side_peephole.beats:
Early May, late afternoon after hero training, by the locker rooms at U.A. Academy. The class has come in hot and tired from the training ground, and Minoru Mineta is with the player as everyone splits up to change.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: in the Men's Locker Room, Mineta finds a small hole bored through the shared wall, and his excitement fills the room. Tenya Iida orders him to stop at once; Mineta declares the hole a treasure left by the students who came before and leans in. He never gets a look. Before his eye reaches it, Kyoka Jiro's earphone jack shoots through the hole from the far side and jabs him square in the eye. Mineta drops to the floor howling, and through the wall Jiro's flat voice says the hole is taken care of.

A man in the class can try to drag Mineta away first, back Iida, block the hole with a towel or a locker, or simply watch the punishment land. Whatever he does, nobody sees anything through the wall and the narration never describes the other side.

If the player is a woman, she is on the other side, changing with Jiro in the Women's Locker Room: she hears Mineta's muffled boasting through the wall, sees Jiro's jack slide into the little hole, and hears the yelp. She can help plug the hole for good and decide whether to report it to Shota Aizawa.

Mineta recovers with a watering eye, a long sulk and no sympathy from anyone.

The event is complete when Mineta has been stopped and the hole is plugged or reported, or the party leaves.

side_afo_talk.title: All Might's Story
side_afo_talk.beats:
Early May, late in the day after hero training, at U.A. Academy. Izuku Midoriya is with the player, and so is the tall adult who has come looking for him: All Might, or the thin, tired man Toshinori Yagi if he is the one standing there. Whichever of them it is asks Izuku, quietly and seriously, for a word in private, and leads him off toward the Teachers' Lounge.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the talk is private and stays private. The door closes, the voices beyond it are low, and nothing carries; the narration never reports what is said, never guesses at it and never follows Izuku inside. The player can wait in the hall, go back to the others, or try to listen; a listener hears only the hum of a vending machine before a passing teacher moves them along. A good while later Izuku comes back alone. He is quieter than when he left, hands clenched, eyes on something far away, and asked about it he says only that it was about Hosu and his internship, then changes the subject with a smile that does not quite hold. The player can press him, leave him be, or nudge him back to normal.

Then Shota Aizawa finds the class with an announcement in his flat drawl: summer break is coming, and Class 1-A will spend part of it at a training camp in the forest, for everyone who passes the final exams; anyone who fails spends those days in remedial lessons instead. The room erupts in plans, and Aizawa tells everyone to calm down.

By path: a Class 1-A student lives the scene above. A faculty member sees the request made, may be asked to keep the lounge clear for a while and does so without asking why, then walks with Aizawa when he goes to give his class the news.

The event is complete when Izuku is back and Aizawa has announced the summer camp, or the party leaves.

side_hot_spring_wall.title: The Hot Spring Wall
side_hot_spring_wall.beats:
The first night of the forest training camp, bath time at the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge. The classes have survived Beast's Forest and dinner, and the outdoor Hot Spring Bath is split down the middle by a tall wooden divider, the men on one side and the women on the other. Minoru Mineta is with the player and has been eyeing that divider since he arrived.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Mineta announces his plan, plucks his sticky spheres and starts to climb. On top of the divider sits Kota Izumi, a small child, fully dressed and posted there as a lookout by the Pussycats; he saw this coming. With one scornful word he shoves Mineta off, and Mineta drops back into the water on the men's side with a huge splash. Nobody sees anything over the wall, and the narration never looks over it. A cheer of thanks goes up from the women's side, Kota startles, his foot slips on the wet top of the wall, and he tips backward toward the stones. Izuku Midoriya is already moving: he flares Full Cowl and catches him clean out of the air. Kota is unhurt; he only goes still and pale for a moment. Izuku hurries him to Mandalay in the Lodge Hall, and she thanks him and keeps Kota close.

A man in the class can try to talk Mineta down before he starts, pull him off the wall, or help steady the catch; nobody is ever in more danger than that one slip. If the player is a woman, she is on the other side of the divider: she hears Mineta's scheme, Kota's sharp voice and the splash, joins the thanks or not, and hears about the catch afterward.

The event is complete when Kota is safe with Mandalay and Mineta has been fished out and scolded, or the party leaves.

side_boot_camp.title: Quirk Boot Camp
side_boot_camp.beats:
The second day of the forest training camp, in the training grounds of the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge. From first light Shota Aizawa and Vlad King have both classes in the Training Clearing, and the rule is simple: push a Quirk past its limit, again and again, until the limit moves. Pixie-Bob raises terrain on demand, Ragdoll's Search tracks every student at once and gleefully calls out weak points, Mandalay's Telepathy relays orders, and Tiger drills anyone with a body-strengthening Quirk in close combat until they drop.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: the clearing becomes a festival of suffering. Katsuki Bakugo plunges his hands into near-boiling water between blasts. Shoto Todoroki stands in a drum bath, trading ice and fire to keep the water bearable. Ochaco Uraraka rolls herself around inside a huge ball to beat her own nausea, until she is sick in the bushes. Eijiro Kirishima and Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu harden side by side while being struck, racing to crack last. Yuga Aoyama fires his laser until his stomach gives out. Denki Kaminari draws current from an enormous battery. Rikido Sato studies while eating sugar by the fistful. Koji Koda calls animals until he is hoarse. The player gets a drill of their own, built on their Quirk's real weak point: they can throw themselves into it, find a smarter angle, help a classmate through theirs, or complain, which only earns another set.

Before the day ends, Aizawa reminds the students headed for remedial lessons (by default Kaminari, Mina Ashido, Kirishima, Sato and Hanta Sero, unless the exams went differently) that their extra lessons start tonight, with Neito Monoma joining from Class 1-B. A player who failed joins them.

By path: a Class 1-A student trains under Aizawa's eye; a Class 1-B student trains under Vlad King's beside the 1-A rivals, with Itsuka Kendo keeping her class in line.

The event is complete when the drills end for the day and the remedial list has been read, or the party leaves.

side_curry_night.title: Curry Night
side_curry_night.beats:
The second day of the forest training camp, late afternoon at the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge. Around four o'clock the drills are done, both classes are starving, and Pixie-Bob and Ragdoll herd everyone to the Outdoor Kitchen with a cheerful announcement: last night's dinner was the only one the Pussycats cook. From now on the students make their own, and tonight it is curry.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Tenya Iida turns it into a lesson at once, declaring that feeding people in a disaster zone is hero work too, and starts assigning stations. Shoto Todoroki lights every stove with a flick of fire and keeps being asked to light more. Katsuki Bakugo chops vegetables with alarming speed and precision and snarls at anyone who looks surprised. Momo Yaoyorozu creates whatever utensil is missing, Ochaco Uraraka floats the heaviest pots, someone burns the rice and someone else saves it. Class 1-B has its own pots going a few tables down, and the rivalry carries straight into whose curry is better. The player can cook, run a station, mess with a rival pot in fun, or watch Bakugo's knife work in silent awe.

The default ending: plates full under the trees as the light goes, both classes too tired to talk, and everyone agreeing it is the best meal of their lives.

By path: a Class 1-A student cooks under Iida's stations and beside Bakugo's knife; a Class 1-B student cooks with Itsuka Kendo keeping order and Neito Monoma insisting 1-B's curry is the refined one.

The event is complete when the curry is served and eaten, or the party leaves.

side_kota_cliff.title: Kota's Secret Cliff
side_kota_cliff.beats:
The second night of the forest training camp, after the curry dinner, around the Wild Wild Pussycats Lodge and the woods above it. Kota Izumi, a small child, skipped the meal and slipped away, and Izuku Midoriya noticed. He fills a plate and sets off up the Hidden Cliff Path after him, toward the rock ledge Kota thinks nobody knows about.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: if the player is with Izuku, they can go with him, carry a second plate, or let him go alone and wait. At Kota's Rock Ledge the child sits with his back to the camp, watching the mountains in the dusk. He wants neither the curry nor the company. He tells Izuku to go away, and then, bitter, that heroes and villains are all the same: people showing off their Quirks, and his parents died for nothing because of it. Izuku does not argue with the grief. He tells Kota about a friend of his who was born without a Quirk, who was told all his life that he could never be a hero, and who wanted it anyway. Kota does not answer. Izuku sets the plate on the rock, says it is there if he gets hungry, and walks back down. The narration never says who the friend was.

If the player is with Kota instead, they found his ledge first or followed him up; Kota is curt and wants them gone, and Izuku arrives with the plate soon after. The player can stay quiet, speak up for Kota or for Izuku, or leave him in peace.

Kota is a child throughout: the ledge is his safe spot, nobody grabs him or frightens him, and nothing dangerous happens tonight.

The event is complete when Izuku has left the curry and walked back down to the lodge, or the party leaves.

side_traitor_meeting.title: Is There a Traitor?
side_traitor_meeting.beats:
The day after the villain attack on the forest training camp, at U.A. Academy. The faculty with the player have gathered behind a closed door, in the Teachers' Lounge or wherever they stand, worn out from the hospital, the police and the phones. Katsuki Bakugo is in the League's hands unless the raid ended differently, and the question in the room is how the League knew where to strike.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: Present Mic says out loud what several of them are thinking: the camp's location was kept quiet, so it may have leaked from inside. Snipe pushes back hard: start a mole hunt among colleagues and students now, and the school tears itself apart at the worst possible moment. Voices rise. Principal Nezu lets them run for a while, then says calmly that he trusts everyone in this room, and that the work in front of them is getting the students back and keeping the rest safe. Before anyone can answer, a phone call comes for All Might: if he is in the room he steps out to take it, and if not, word arrives that the police have called him and he has gone. The meeting loses its thread.

The player is a member of the faculty with a real voice here: they can argue for a quiet inquiry, side with Snipe, propose concrete security steps, back Nezu, or ask about the call (the answer is only that the police are moving). No traitor is named, no suspect is singled out and nobody accuses a student; the question stays open. If Shota Aizawa, Vlad King or Nemuri Kayama are in the room, they say little and are visibly short of sleep.

The event is complete when the call has broken up the meeting and the question is left open, or the party leaves.

side_rescue_plan.title: The Rescue Plan
side_rescue_plan.beats:
Early August, a few days after the forest camp raid, at Musutafu General Hospital. Class 1-A has come to see the classmates still laid up from the raid, Izuku Midoriya among them with both arms bandaged, and Eijiro Kirishima is with the player. He has not been himself since the camp: he keeps going back to the moment Katsuki Bakugo was carried off and his own hand closed on empty air. If the raid ended with nobody taken, the scene is only Kirishima admitting how close it came, and no plan forms.

Default course, as pressure the player can change: with the door shut, in Izuku's room in the Patient Rooms or wherever the visitors have gathered, Kirishima says it plainly: the pros are on it, but he cannot sit and wait; he wants to go and get Bakugo back. Shoto Todoroki stands with him. Then Momo Yaoyorozu, still recovering from the raid, reveals that during the fight she created a tracker and Yosetsu Awase welded it onto the Nomu that attacked them; the police know, and she could build a receiver for its signal. The room goes quiet. Tenya Iida stands against it, firmly: they are students without licenses, the pros and police already have this, and charging in is how more classmates get hurt. Tsuyu Asui agrees with him, frank and shaken, and most of the class sides with Iida. Kirishima does not back down; he says he will leave from the hospital tomorrow night with anyone willing, and asks Momo to think about the receiver.

The player has a real voice: back Kirishima, object with Iida and Tsuyu, look for a middle path, or say nothing. Telling a teacher is the player's call; by default the students keep it among themselves. Nobody leaves today: the departure belongs to tomorrow night.

The event is complete when the argument ends with Kirishima's plan on the table and the class divided, or the party leaves.

side_like_midoriya.title: Midoriya or Iida?
side_like_midoriya.beats:
An evening at U.A. Academy in late summer, in the weeks of ultimate-move training, wherever the party is with Ochaco Uraraka and Mina Ashido (most often the Class 1-A Dorm Lounge after a long day in Gym Gamma). Everyone is sore, the snacks are out, and Mina has spent days watching Ochaco drift off mid-conversation.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Mina flops down beside Ochaco and asks, loud enough for the whole room, which one it is: Midoriya or Iida? Ochaco's composure goes and her Zero Gravity goes with it. She floats off the floor, arms windmilling, denying everything at once: they are friends, good friends, the best of friends, and Mina has it all wrong. Mina takes every denial as proof and grins wider. When Ochaco finally drifts back down, she laughs it off and changes the subject. Then, in a quiet moment the narration only shows, she looks at her hands, sets her jaw and settles something with herself: whatever that feeling is, it waits until she is a hero. It stays a look and a small nod, never a confession, and nobody in the room hears it said aloud.

The party has a real part: join Mina's teasing, catch Ochaco by the ankle before she reaches the ceiling, rescue her with a new topic, or become Mina's next target when she turns the same question on the party. If Izuku Midoriya or Tenya Iida walks in mid-question, Ochaco lands hard and bolts for the women's wing. Romance stays a hint; the comedy is the point.

By path: a Class 1-A party is in the room as a classmate, a witness Mina can recruit or a target she can switch to, and can make the moment kinder or louder.

The event is complete when Ochaco is back on the floor and the subject has changed, by her hand, Mina's or the party's.

side_second_term.title: The Second-Term Opening Ceremony
side_second_term.beats:
The morning of the first day of the second term at U.A. Academy, in mid-September, when the bell calls every course out to the Athletics Field for the opening ceremony. The Hero Course, General Studies, the Support Course and the Management Course form their lines on the field, with the faculty along the side of the stage. Class 1-A's line has two gaps: Izuku Midoriya and Katsuki Bakugo fought on campus last night and are confined to the dorm, and neither appears at the ceremony at all.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: in Class 1-B's line, Neito Monoma leans across the gap to gloat that Class 1-A lost two of its own at the license exam, Bakugo and Todoroki, while every member of 1-B passed; Itsuka Kendo cuts him off with a chop. Shoto Todoroki stands in 1-A's line and takes it without a word. On the stage, Principal Nezu's speech wanders from the dorms and the year's hard news into how his diet and daily routine have been off since the summer, before he finds his point: U.A. must keep the public's trust, and every student carries a share of it. Then Hound Dog steps up about last night's fight. He starts in calm words, his anger climbs and the rest comes out as growls and barks; another teacher gives the short version: no fighting, and follow the dorm rules.

By path: a Class 1-A party stands beside the gaps, fields questions about them and can answer Monoma, back Todoroki or keep quiet. A Class 1-B party is in Monoma's line and can egg him on or help Kendo stop him. A General Studies party watches the Hero Course bicker from outside, Hitoshi Shinso dry beside it. A Support Course or Management Course party hears the rumors in the back rows and can trade theories or spot the story in two empty places. A Faculty party stands with the teachers and may be the one who translates Hound Dog.

The event is complete when the ceremony ends and the courses are dismissed to their homerooms.

side_ryukyu.title: Ryukyu Says Yes
side_ryukyu.beats:
A late-September day, wherever the party is with Ochaco Uraraka, Tsuyu Asui or Nejire Hado. The two first-years' old internship hosts have passed on taking them for work-studies, so Nejire has done what she does best: asked questions until she found an answer. Her own agency head, the Dragoon Hero Ryukyu, has come to look the two over in person, and the meeting is under way where they are: Ryukyu calm and polite, Nejire firing questions, Ochaco and Tsuyu trying very hard to be impressive.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Ryukyu is kind and not yet convinced; she already has one student and takes the job of raising young heroes seriously. Then an alarm breaks the talk: in the Musutafu Station District near U.A. (its Station Concourse and the Hero Merch Arcade, a short walk from campus; this is Musutafu, not Hosu) two villains with Gigantification swell to building height and start tearing at the storefronts. Ryukyu clears civilians and watches. Nejire takes the air, Ochaco floats debris and a stalled car clear, Tsuyu pulls people out of the way with her tongue, and together the three bring both giants down. Afterward Ryukyu says yes to both of them.

The party can fight beside them, cover the civilians, take one giant alone or hold back and let the students prove themselves. If the party does not go with them, the moment passes and the news comes back that evening.

By path: a Class 1-A party with a provisional license acts under Ryukyu's eye; if it has no placement yet, she may weigh the party as well. A Licensed Pro Hero party is a working pro on that street and can take command or let the students handle it, and Ryukyu asks the party's read on them afterward. A Licensed Sidekick party is on its agency's beat and works the scene beside them as an equal.

The event is complete when both giants are down and Ryukyu has given her answer, or the party parts from the three before the trouble starts.

side_quiet_week.title: The Quiet Week
side_quiet_week.beats:
A weekday in mid-October at U.A. Academy, wherever the party is with Izuku Midoriya, Eijiro Kirishima, Ochaco Uraraka or Tsuyu Asui. The four work-study students have been on call for days under orders from their agencies to say nothing about the case they are on. Kirishima's grin is forced, Ochaco and Tsuyu change the subject together, and Izuku has barely spoken since a patrol nobody else in the class knows about: he picks at his food, stares at his hands and apologizes for nothing.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: at the next meal (lunch in Lunch Rush's Cafeteria, or dinner in the dorm if the day is done) Tenya Iida sits down across from Izuku and, formal and earnest, reminds him that friends are there for exactly the moments a person is stuck, secret details or not. Shoto Todoroki slides his tray of cold soba over and says, plainly, that heroes are allowed to cry. Izuku manages a small, real smile and eats. Nothing about the case is said.

The party has a real part: press for details and hit the wall of the blackout, respect the silence, keep Izuku company, or be the one who gets him to eat. The four hold their orders: no names, no places, no case. If the live story has already changed how Izuku's last patrol ended, play the strain of waiting under the blackout rather than guilt.

By path: a Class 1-A party is a classmate at the table. If the party is itself on a work-study tied to the case, it is under the same order, and its friends' questions land on it too.

The event is complete when Izuku eats with his friends, or the party leaves the four to their silence.

side_interns_home.title: The Interns Come Home
side_interns_home.beats:
Late at night in late October at Heights Alliance, two or three days after the Shie Hassaikai raid, wherever the party is with Izuku Midoriya, Eijiro Kirishima, Ochaco Uraraka or Tsuyu Asui. The four work-study students have just come back through the dorm door after hospital waiting rooms, paperwork and hours of police questions. The lounge lights are still on, and Class 1-A has been waiting up.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the class surrounds them at once. Mina Ashido is close to tears, everyone talks over everyone, and there are too many questions and too much relief for one room. Tenya Iida raises his hand, class rep to the end, and asks everyone to be considerate: they are exhausted, so no interrogations tonight. Kirishima laughs and takes the back slaps; Ochaco and Tsuyu lean on each other; Izuku, bandaged, insists he is fine, and keeps insisting. What the four say about the raid stays within what the news and the live story have made known; the narration does not add losses or wounds the live story has not given them.

The party has a real part: welcome them, make tea, press with questions (Iida intervenes), notice that Izuku is not fine, or simply sit with whoever looks the most tired. A party that pushes too hard gets a tired look and the end of the conversation.

By path: a Class 1-A party that stayed on campus is one of the welcoming crowd. A party that was on the raid through its own work-study comes home with the four, gets surrounded too, and can answer, deflect or go straight to bed.

The event is complete when Iida sends everyone to bed, or the party leaves the lounge.

side_eri_tour.title: Eri Visits U.A.
side_eri_tour.beats:
A weekend day off at U.A. Academy in early November, a week before the School Festival, wherever on campus the party is with Eri, Mirio Togata or Izuku Midoriya. With Principal Nezu's approval, Shota Aizawa has brought Eri to see the school early, before the crowds. Mirio leads her tour and Izuku has joined; Aizawa walks a few steps behind. Eri is a small child, a guest of U.A., and the scene stays gentle and warm.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Eri holds Mirio's sleeve and says very little. Class 1-A greets her with careful, quiet hellos. In the Main Gymnasium, Class 1-B is rehearsing its play, and Neito Monoma brags that it will outshine anything the class next door puts on. In the Courtyard, Nejire Hado swoops in with a dozen questions, and Mirio steers her gently away from the horn. In the Development Studio, Mei Hatsume's newest suit pops in a cloud of harmless smoke; Eri flinches, and Mirio turns it into a joke. Lunch is in Lunch Rush's Cafeteria, with Principal Nezu at a nearby table over tea and Nemuri Kayama stopping to wave hello. Eri asks small questions about the festival. She does not smile yet; that is still ahead.

The party has a real part: walk beside her, answer at her level, show her its own corner of campus, or keep the noise and the crowds away. Nobody asks her about the past or about her Quirk, and Aizawa stays close. If the live story never freed Eri, this visit does not happen.

By path: a Class 1-A party joins the tour. A Class 1-B party is in the rehearsal and can show her a piece of the play. A Faculty party is on duty with Aizawa, clearing routes and keeping the visit calm.

The event is complete when lunch is over and Aizawa takes Eri home to rest, or the party says goodbye to the tour.

side_aoyama_cheese.title: Cheese at the Door
side_aoyama_cheese.beats:
An evening at U.A. Academy in early November, in the busy week of festival preparations, wherever the party is with Izuku Midoriya or Yuga Aoyama. For days Aoyama has been strange around Izuku: at lunch he shoved a piece of cheese into Izuku's mouth without a word and swept away, at night he watches from the dorm balcony, and tonight Izuku found cheese laid out at his door to spell two words: I know.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Izuku is baffled and a little alarmed. After the evening's training and rehearsal for Class 1-A's festival show, where Aoyama has the sparkling centerpiece, too much Navel Laser doubles him over with stomach pain; he tries to hide it behind a pose. Izuku helps him somewhere quiet (a bench in the Heights Alliance Yard or an empty hallway). There, pale and plain-spoken for once, Aoyama explains: when he was very young his body could not handle his Quirk, every beam hurt, and the belt is what made it usable. He says he sees the same in Izuku, a power the body has to fight to hold, and the cheese was his clumsy way of saying so. Izuku takes it as an odd kindness, and the two agree to shine at the festival.

The party has a real part: laugh about the cheese with Izuku, help Aoyama to the bench, stand guard, or tease him. If the party presses on what I know means, Aoyama sparkles, says non, non, and changes the subject. The narration never explains how he could know anything, never links him to anyone outside U.A., and never hints at more than odd behavior.

By path: a Class 1-A party is a classmate who saw the cheese, the pain or both.

The event is complete when Aoyama's pain eases and he and Izuku part on good terms, or the party leaves them to it.

side_ofa_three.title: Bakugo Joins the Talks
side_ofa_three.beats:
Early December at U.A. Academy, a few days after the Joint Training, wherever the party is with Izuku Midoriya and Katsuki Bakugo, on the Gym Gamma Training Floor or anywhere on campus with room to move. Since the training, when black tendrils lashed out of Izuku's arms in front of both classes, Bakugo has watched him with narrowed eyes. Today he has run out of patience: he wants to see it again.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: Bakugo forces a spar (if they are indoors, he drags Izuku out to the Heights Alliance Yard or the gym floor). They go at it hard; Izuku reaches for the tendrils and gets a flicker, then nothing, and Bakugo pushes harder. Then All Might, thin and retired, arrives and stops it with a single raised voice: Young Midoriya, Young Bakugo, enough. He asks them both to come with him, and the three talk apart, behind the glass of the Gym Gamma Observation Deck or out of earshot across the yard.

The party watches from a distance: Izuku talking with his hands, Bakugo scowling, then very still, All Might grave. What is said stays theirs. The narration never voices it, never names a Quirk's history and never explains the tendrils. If the party tries to follow or listen, All Might kindly asks for privacy, and Bakugo far less kindly. When they come back, Izuku looks lighter, and Bakugo tells anyone who asks to butt out.

The party has a real part before that: spar with them, referee, call for a teacher, or step back.

By path: a Class 1-A party is a classmate who saw the tendrils at the Joint Training and can be the one who asks, or the one who chooses not to.

The event is complete when the three come back from their private talk, or the party leaves before All Might arrives.

side_survival_training.title: Do-or-Die Survival Training
side_survival_training.beats:
A late-summer day at Ground Beta, in the weeks before the provisional license exam, wherever on the mock city the party is with Class 1-A. Shota Aizawa is running a rescue exercise beneath it: a damaged six-floor underground mall built for disaster drills, entered through a hatch by the Mock City Central Plaza, with dummies for casualties and a hard clock. Team A goes down first: Izuku Midoriya, Katsuki Bakugo, Shoto Todoroki, Tenya Iida, Ochaco Uraraka and more of the class. The rest wait on the surface as Team B, and Aizawa watches the feeds from the Monitoring Room.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: the drill runs well until a real collapse nobody planned. Stairwells fold, the radios die and Team A is cut off several floors down. Iida is hurt in the collapse and has to be carried. Ochaco floats rubble aside, and the others shore up the ceiling and scout the dark. Then a broken water main floods the lower floors. The team carries Iida up the last open route, and Izuku, Bakugo and Todoroki, the final three below, ride the pressurized water up a shaft and burst out onto the surface. Nobody dies, and every injury heals later in the infirmary.

The collapse always comes; how they get out is up to the party: carry Iida, find the route, hold the water back, take the last ride up, or (on the surface) dig, relay and guide the rescue with Aizawa.

By path: a Class 1-A party chooses its team at the hatch. On Team A it is trapped with them; on Team B it is the rescue from above, and the stakes are the same.

The event is complete when every student is back on the surface and Aizawa calls the exercise, or the party leaves Ground Beta before the collapse.

side_tokoyami_winter.title: Tokoyami's Winter Work-Study
side_tokoyami_winter.beats:
A December day at the Hawks Hero Agency in Fukuoka, during the winter work-studies, wherever in the agency the party is with Fumikage Tokoyami. Tokoyami, hero name Tsukuyomi, has come back for the winter. Last time Hawks cleared every incident before he could arrive; this time Hawks is hardly here, busy elsewhere, and the agency's sidekicks run the shifts. Tokoyami works as one of them: callouts in the Hawks Agency Operations Room, launches from the Hawks Agency Rooftop, and fast flights over the city with Dark Shadow.

Canon default course, as pressure the player can change: a callout comes in (a worker stranded on a high ledge, or a thief running the rooftops) and the sidekicks give it to Tokoyami with the party. He handles it cleanly, Dark Shadow muttering commentary. Back on the rooftop, Hawks drops in between errands, hears the report, and for the first time talks to Tokoyami as a partner: he asks for his read, hands him a task of his own and calls him Tsukuyomi. Then he is gone again. Where Hawks goes and why stays his business; the narration does not explain or hint.

The party has a real part: fly the callout with Tokoyami, cover him from the ground, argue a better plan, or let him lead and watch him grow.

By path: a Class 1-A party is also on work-study at the agency and shares the shifts, part rival and part partner. A Licensed Pro Hero party is a visiting pro with business at the agency or on a joint operation; Hawks may ask its honest read of his work-study student. A Licensed Sidekick party is one of the agency's sidekicks, or one on loan from another agency, and works beside Tokoyami as an equal.

The event is complete when Hawks has dropped in, spoken to Tokoyami as a partner and left again, or when the party leaves the agency at the end of that day.
